DETAILED DESCRIPTION
1. Construction of C(r,N)
[0019] Let r ≥ 2 be an integer (the number of parity rows) and let N satisfy 1 ≤ N ≤ 2^(r−1) − 1
(the number of message symbols). An integer m in 0 … 2^r − 1 is identified with the binary rvector whose row k is bit k of m (bit 0 is the least significant bit). The parity-check matrix H
(100, FIG. 1) is the r-by-N binary matrix whose j-th column (0-indexed) is the j-th such vector,
taken in increasing integer order, among those with bit 0 set and Hamming weight at least two;
equivalently, the odd integers 3, 5, 7, … in increasing order.
3

 [0020] The bound on N follows by counting: there are 2^(r−1) binary r-vectors with bit 0 set;
excluding the weight-one vector (bit 0 alone) leaves 2^(r−1) − 1 admissible columns.
[0021] Every column of H contains bit 0, shown as common-bit row 102 in FIG. 1; rows 1
through r−1 are shown as rows 104 and the columns as columns 106. Example: C(7,48) is the
[55,48] code with 7 parity rows protecting 48 message symbols; its columns are the odd integers
3 through 97.
2. Decoder
[0022] Referring to FIG. 3, given a received word with payload estimate v′ (N real values) and
parity estimate t′ (r real values), and, in the confirmed embodiment, a received confirmation
symbol u′, the decoder performs the following steps.
[0023] (i) Step 302: compute the syndrome s = H·v′ − t′.
[0024] (ii) Step 304: in the confirmed embodiment, compute the confirmation residual q = Σ_j
w_j·v′_j − u′, where w_0 … w_(N−1) are pairwise distinct nonzero weights and the transmitted
confirmation symbol is u = Σ_j w_j·v_j. In a preferred embodiment w_j = (j + 1)^2. The weights
are preferably not an affine function of the column integer: because the column vectors are
binary, any relation a·H_i + b·H_j + c·H_k = d·H_l among columns also holds among the
column integers, so weights affine in the column integer (for example w_j = j + 1, which equals
(m_j − 1)/2 for column integer m_j) give no additional protection against such relations, whereas
squared weights did in the tested range (section 4).
[0025] (iii) Step 306: if every component of s is zero and q is zero, output CLEAN (308). If s is
zero and q is nonzero, output CONFIRMATION_EDIT: the confirmation symbol alone was
altered and the payload passes all r parity checks.
[0026] (iv) Step 310: let supp(s) be the set of rows where s is nonzero. If supp(s) equals the
support of exactly one column j, all nonzero components of s equal a common value c, and (in
the confirmed embodiment) q = c·w_j, subtract c from v′_j, recompute the syndrome, and output
REPAIRED (312) only if the recomputed syndrome is zero; otherwise output REFUSED.
[0027] (v) Step 314: if supp(s) is a single row k, then in the confirmed embodiment (step 316)
output TAIL_EDIT (318, payload intact) only if q = 0 and otherwise output REFUSED; in the

4

 unconfirmed embodiment output REFUSED, the parity fault being detected but the payload not
accepted.
[0028] (vi) Step 320: otherwise output REFUSED, store a refusal record (322) comprising at
least the syndrome, and take no corrective action.
[0029] "Zero" in a floating-point implementation means magnitude not exceeding a tolerance
TOL fixed in advance (for example 1e−9 relative to the largest payload magnitude). The
guarantees of section 3 are stated for exact arithmetic and hold in floating point for faults whose
magnitudes, and whose differences of weighted contributions, exceed TOL.
3. Guarantees (exact arithmetic)
[0030] The following hold for every instance C(r,N).
[0031] (a) Single payload spike. A spike of nonzero magnitude e at position j yields s = e·H_j
and q = e·w_j. The support equals that of column j only, because the columns are distinct; the
values are uniform; and the decoder outputs REPAIRED with the payload restored.
[0032] (b) Single parity edit. An edit of magnitude f at parity row k yields s = −f·e_k and q = 0.
Every column has weight at least two, so no column matches; the confirmed decoder outputs
TAIL_EDIT and the unconfirmed decoder outputs REFUSED.
[0033] (c) Two payload spikes. Let a and b be nonzero reals, i ≠ j, and s = a·H_i + b·H_j. (c1) s
is never zero, since s_p equals a or b at any row p lying in exactly one of the two supports, and
such a row exists because the columns are distinct. (c2) s never equals a uniform multiple of a
column. If a ≠ b and a ≠ −b, the common value would have to be a or b at a row in exactly one
support, while row 0 carries a + b, which differs from both. If a = b, row 0 carries 2a while a row
in exactly one support carries a. If a = −b, row 0 carries 0, but every column contains row 0. (c3)
s has exactly one nonzero row if and only if a = −b and H_i and H_j differ in exactly one row. If
a ≠ −b, row 0 is nonzero and any other row p of H_i, which exists because H_i has weight at
least two, carries a or a + b, both nonzero, so at least two rows are nonzero. If a = −b, s = a·(H_i
− H_j), supported exactly on the rows where the columns differ.
[0034] Consequently, with the unconfirmed decoder every two-spike fault is REFUSED; with
the confirmed decoder, in case (c3) q = a·(w_i − w_j) ≠ 0, so the fault is REFUSED, and in all
other cases (c1) and (c2) give REFUSED. A decoder that instead outputs TAIL_EDIT for every
5

 single-row syndrome without confirmation would misclassify exactly the pairs of case (c3); for
C(7,48) there are 124 such column pairs out of 1,128. FIG. 7 shows the smallest instance: in
C(3,3) the columns are 3 = rows {0,1} (702), 5 = rows {0,2} (704), and 7 = rows {0,1,2} (706)
in the support lattice 700; spikes +e at column 3 and −e at column 7 give s = (0, 0, −e), a singlerow syndrome on row 2 (708), and columns 5 and 7 likewise give a single-row syndrome on row
1, whereas columns 3 and 5 differ in two rows and give a two-row syndrome.
[0035] (d) Same-sign faults. For k ≥ 2 spikes at distinct positions with magnitudes all strictly
positive or all strictly negative, row 0 carries the total and every other row of the union of
supports carries a nonzero partial sum, so s has at least two nonzero rows; uniformity would
require every row of the union to lie in every faulted column, contradicting distinctness. The
fault is REFUSED. For C(7,48), all 17,296 triples of distinct columns were also checked: no
combination of three columns with same-sign nonzero amplitudes equals a multiple of any
column.
[0036] (e) Disclosed boundary. Mixed-sign faults of three or more spikes can produce a
syndrome equal to a uniform multiple of a single column. Example: +1 at the columns for 11 and
13 and −1 at the column for 9 give the syndrome of column 15. Such relations are structural. For
C(7,48), 13,060 of the 17,296 triples of distinct columns have a bitwise exclusive-or equal to a
fourth column, and 7,140 of those triples admit nonzero real amplitudes a1, a2, a3 with a1·H_i +
a2·H_j + a3·H_k equal to the fourth column exactly. An exclusive-or triple (i, j, k) admits such
amplitudes exactly when one of the three supports lies between the intersection and the union of
the other two (for example S_i ∩ S_j ⊆ S_k ⊆ S_i ∪ S_j); this sandwich condition agreed with
the real-amplitude test for all 13,060 exclusive-or triples of C(7,48). Without a confirmation
value, a fault with such amplitudes would be repaired to the wrong column. With squared
weights, the confirmed decoder refused every three-spike fault in the exhaustively tested range of
section 4; this is a measured result for that range, not a proof, and mixed-sign faults of three or
more spikes remain outside the guaranteed fault model.

Counts below are summed over every N for each r.

[0040] For C(7,48): every single spike is repaired; every single parity edit is classified; all 1,128

5. RFF-1 Self-Describing Frame Format
[0041] Referring to FIG. 4, a frame 400 comprises, in order: a magic field 402 of 4 bytes, value
0x52464631 (ASCII "RFF1"); a field 404 of 1 byte giving the parity-row count r, 2 ≤ r; a field
406 of 2 bytes, unsigned big-endian, giving the message-symbol count N, 1 ≤ N ≤ 2^(r−1) − 1; a
field 408 of 1 byte giving the lane count L, 1 ≤ L, where L divides N; a payload 410 of N
IEEE-754 binary64 values, big-endian, where lane l (0-indexed) holds symbols l·N/L through
(l+1)·N/L − 1; a parity field 412 of r IEEE-754 binary64 values, big-endian, equal to H·payload;
and, in the confirmed embodiment, a confirmation field 414 of one further IEEE-754 binary64
value u = Σ_j w_j·payload_j, with w_j = j + 1 unless otherwise signaled.
[0042] In a version-2 variant, the magic field is 0xD2464631 (0x52464631 with bit 31 set) and
the payload, parity, and confirmation values are IEEE-754 binary32; a receiver implementing
only version 1 refuses a frame whose magic field it does not recognize.
[0043] A receiver parses the header, reconstructs H from (r, N) by the construction of section 1,
and decodes the frame per section 2. A header with r, N, or L outside the stated ranges is refused.
6. Two-Layer Refusal System
7

 [0044] Referring to FIG. 5, in Layer 1 (code layer 502) each received frame from channel 500 is
decoded per section 2, yielding CLEAN, REPAIRED, TAIL_EDIT, CONFIRMATION_EDIT,
or REFUSED. Frames output as REFUSED are recorded in refusal store 504 and are not passed
to Layer 2. Frames output as REPAIRED are passed with the corrected payload; frames output as
CLEAN, TAIL_EDIT, or CONFIRMATION_EDIT are passed with the received payload.
[0045] In Layer 2 (admission layer 506), each frame passed by Layer 1 is partitioned into its L
lanes. For each lane, a claimed figure C_i and an interior figure I_i are retained under a label i
unique within the lane's record, a label-specific headroom H_i = I_i − C_i is computed, and the
lane is admitted (508) only if every required label has a corresponding interior label and H_i ≥ 0
for every required label; otherwise the lane is refused (510). A surplus at one label or lane is not
applied to a deficit at another label or lane. Each admission or refusal is written as a new
decision record without overwriting the input records (see U.S. Provisional Application No.
64/169,264).
7. Instances and Overhead
[0046] Referring to FIG. 6, the following instances were constructed: C(6,31), a [37,31] code
with overhead 16.2%, 465 column pairs, of which 75 differ in exactly one row; C(7,48), a

 ABSTRACT
A fault-refusing error-correction code family C(r,N) uses an r-by-N binary parity-check matrix
whose columns are the odd integers 3, 5, 7, and onward in increasing order, read as binary rvectors, so every column shares row 0 and has weight at least two. A repair-or-refuse decoder
repairs a single payload fault only on a unique uniform column match confirmed by a zero
recomputed syndrome, accepts a single-row syndrome as a parity edit only when an independent
confirmation value shows the payload unaltered, and otherwise refuses and records the refusal.
Every fault of two payload spikes at distinct positions, of any magnitudes and signs, is refused. A
self-describing frame format carries the parameters, lanes, payload, and parity, and a two-layer
system bars code-refused frames from per-lane headroom admission.

# Monsters Ink LLC: Competition & Product Definition
*Internal report. Prepared Oct 15, 2026 (CT). Not for external distribution. Leaves out RFF-1 and decoder-fix specifics on purpose.*

## Bottom line
- **Your competition is free, built-in, already-deployed tooling.** Nobody is selling a "refusal-first admission/ECC" product, but buyers already get "good enough" versions for free in Kubernetes, Envoy, Netflix's library, SEC-DED/Chipkill memory, and open-source lock-free queues.
- **What you can actually sell today (TRL ~4):** (1) paid technical briefs and assurance consulting, and (2) SBIR/STTR Phase I proposals that turn the ideas into a TRL 5–6 demo. Patent licensing or an IP sale only becomes realistic **after** the patents are granted or published as non-provisionals **and** there is a benchmarked reference implementation.
- **Where the novelty is (honest view):** not in "detect and refuse" alone, which SEC-DED already does. The novel part is **pairing** a formal admission invariant (C+R ≤ I(t), with a seal) with **lane-level refusal** that carries ECC/fault ambiguity up into the scheduling and admission decision. That cross-layer "refuse instead of guessing" story is the claim to defend.

## (a) Competitors and prior approaches

### 1. Headroom admission control (64/150,688) and Members Gate (64/169,264)
| Incumbent | What it does (sourced) | Better than yours | Worse / your angle |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Kubernetes ResourceQuota admission** ([docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/policy/resource-quotas/)) | Caps aggregate per-namespace requests and limits. A request that breaks quota is rejected with HTTP 403. Quotas are static and "independent of the cluster capacity"; dynamic policies require "writing a 'controller'". | Universal, free, battle-tested, integrated with RBAC and ValidatingAdmissionPolicy | Static ceilings. Contention is "first-come-first-served". There is no moving ceiling I(t) and no componentwise invariant tied to live capacity. **This gap is your clearest wedge.** |
| **Envoy adaptive concurrency** ([docs](https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/configuration/http/http_filters/adaptive_concurrency_filter)) | Gradient controller: limit_new = gradient·limit_old + headroom, with gradient = (minRTT+B)/sampleRTT and headroom fixed at √limit | Adaptive, production-proven, no model needed | Driven by latency only, one dimension, heuristic. The docs say to expect "a noticeable increase in request 503s" during minRTT windows. It makes no deterministic guarantee. |
| **Netflix concurrency-limits** ([repo](https://github.com/Netflix/concurrency-limits)) | Java library of adaptive limiters in the TCP congestion-control style (Vegas/Gradient) | Free, widely copied | Same: heuristic, latency-driven, no proof object |
| AWS API throttling, token buckets, rate limiters | Fixed rate or burst limits *(general knowledge, not fetched)* | Simple and ubiquitous | Rate is not the same as multi-resource headroom |
| Safety-critical runtime assurance (Simplex architecture, runtime monitors) *(not fetched)* | A verified fallback controller takes over when a monitor trips | Established in avionics and autonomy, with formal pedigree | Monitors switch *controllers*; they don't admit work. **Your closest intellectual competitor in defense.** You need to explain clearly how Headroom differs. |

### 2. Fault-refusing ECC C(r,N) (64/170,360)
| Incumbent | Facts (sourced) | Better than yours | Worse / your angle |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Hamming SEC-DED** ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamming_code)) | Extended Hamming (d=4) corrects 1 error and detects 2. Wikipedia: "some triple errors will be mistaken for single errors and 'corrected' to the wrong value". Common (72,64) and (39,32) forms; Xilinx FPGAs use (72,64). | Fifty-plus years in silicon, minimal overhead, standard | Silent miscorrection at 3 or more errors is a documented weakness. A repair-or-refuse decoder targets exactly this, **but** SEC-DED already *refuses* (flags) double errors. |
| **Chipkill / SDDC / DDDC** ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chipkill)) | IBM Chipkill. Equivalents: Sun Extended ECC, HP Advanced ECC, Intel SDDC/DDDC, Micron RAIN. A Google field study cited there found 8% of DIMMs affected each year. | Handles whole-chip failure. Shipped by every server vendor. | Vendor-locked and in silicon, so a software/IP player can't displace it. You would license into memory-controller IP vendors, which is a long cycle. |
| Reed-Solomon, BCH, LDPC *(not fetched)* | Strong multi-symbol correction for storage and comms | Far stronger correction | Heavy decoders. Bounded-distance decoders already return "decoding failure" for many uncorrectable patterns. |
| CRC + retransmit *(not fetched)* | Detect-only, then resend | Cheap and near-universal | Needs a back-channel; doesn't fit memory or one-way links |

| Boost.Lockfree, Folly MPMCQueue, LMAX Disruptor *(not fetched)* | Mature, heavily benchmarked | Free |
| **Yours** | Hazard pointers plus residual gate plus ceiling tuner | **No independent market.** The tuner shows no benefit on flat workloads and spin_limit had no measurable effect. Position it only as the reference implementation that *demonstrates* Headroom, not as a product. |

**Recommended product statement:** *"Refusal-first runtime assurance: a deterministic admission layer that guarantees load stays under a live resource ceiling and that refuses, rather than guesses, when hardware faults are ambiguous. It ships as briefs and integration services today and as an SDK and licensable IP after SBIR maturation."* Primary buyer: **DoD/NASA program offices and primes that need runtime assurance evidence for autonomous or edge systems.** Secondary: memory/FPGA IP vendors, as licensing later.

## (c) Blunt gaps
1. **Detecting ambiguity is not new.** SEC-DED flags double errors, CRC detects and drops, and RS/BCH report decoding failure. The novelty has to rest on the specific column construction (common bit 0, weight ≥ 2), on guaranteeing refusal for the stated ambiguous classes, and above all on the **two-layer code→admission refusal**. Prove each claim against SEC-DED (72,64) with a fault-injection table.
2. **Headroom vs. a "quota plus controller":** Kubernetes docs already describe building dynamic quotas with a controller. Your differentiator has to be the formal componentwise invariant and the seal (S_H = S_solv ∧ R_H), backed by a proof or model check. A diagram is not enough.
3. **No head-to-head benchmarks** against Envoy, Netflix concurrency-limits, or moodycamel. Without them, technical evaluators default to the free incumbent.
4. **TRL ~4 and a record of unselected outreach.** Evaluators need a hardware-in-the-loop or relevant-environment demo.
5. **SRAT-20's tuner is unproven.** Don't claim performance gains.
6. **Provisional-only status.** Non-provisional deadlines are 12 months from each filing (64/150,688 → Sep 2027). Licensing value depends on getting there.
7. **Market sizes:** this report includes no market-size figures because none were sourced. Don't quote one until you have a cited source.

## 7. Key definitions (lock these)
- **Labeled axis:** a resource identifier unique within a record. Equal counts are not identical figures.
- **C (claimed):** committed allocation per axis. **R (request):** the requested increment. **I(t) (interior/ceiling):** allowed total at decision time. **Reserve Q:** an optional held-back vector, subtracted from I(t). (Use a new letter to avoid the R conflict.)
- **Headroom h_i** = I_i(t) − C_i − R_i, computed per label only.
- **Residual r_H / tolerance ε_H:** define operationally (the measured disagreement between an observed and an expected signal). Do **not** depend on "Howard residual" or "kernel pseudometric" without a full formula.
- **Seal S_H:** true iff every h_i ≥ 0 and |r_H| ≤ ε_H.
- **Refusal purity:** a refused request leaves C bit-identical.
- **Refusal receipt:** an immutable record {request id, timestamp, labels compared, deficits, ceiling snapshot, reason bitmask, previous hash, own hash}.
- **Environment signal, duplicate, BROKE/HELD, weak spot:** define each with a test.

unchanged and emitting a refusal record naming each failing label and its deficit; appending the record to a

mapping the action to a cost vector; applying the Pillar-A seal; on refusal, blocking execution and returning

agents share one I(t); commits are serialized so concurrent admissions never jointly exceed I(t). - 16.
Escalation to human approval when the refusal is within a margin of the ceiling. - 17. Receipts exported in a

while leaving committed work to a separate policy. - 19. Grid/datacenter: price ↑ → power axis ↓. 20.

requests are deferred and re-presented when I(t) rises.

outputting clean, repaired-only-if-the-recomputed-syndrome-is-zero, or refused; forwarding only nonrefused frames to a labeled admission layer that applies the Pillar-A seal per lane; a code-layer refusal never
reaching admission; each layer writing its own receipt. - 25. The code's parity matrix has a common row in

 numeric, negative, missing axis, overflow, NaN); generating an input-validation rule from the BROKE or

test. - 28. Attack log hash-chained and exportable. 29. The rule is installed only if the regression shows zero

refusals (false refusals) from adversarial-source refusals.

## 1. Verdict on the tail-edit flaw
**For two-spike payload faults, the flaw is closed, and that is proved, not just
tested.** It holds for every pair, every sign, and every nonzero real magnitude
(±1…±4 and beyond), in exact arithmetic.
- **Unconfirmed decoder:** every single-row syndrome is refused, so the 124
C(7,48) pairs with a = −b at distance 1 are REFUSED.
- **Confirmed decoder:** q = a(w_i − w_j) ≠ 0 whenever the weights are pairwise
distinct, so those pairs are refused too. This holds for both w = j+1 and w =
(j+1)². Proof (c1)–(c3) is correct.
- **Code check, all real magnitudes (nullspace rank test):** the failure count
was 0 for C(4,7), C(5,15), C(6,31), C(7,48), and C(7,63). C(7,48) has 124 onerow pairs and C(7,63) has 186. The exhaustive ±4 integer run agrees at 0/0 over
24,871,680 events.
**Caveats not covered by the guarantee**
- **Payload spike plus parity edit (two faults).** The unconfirmed decoder
miscorrects 248 of 336 (column, row) combinations in C(7,48) when |f| = |e|. The
confirmed decoder refuses all of them. Rev B's "Need (c) refuses ambiguous
multi-fault patterns" overstates the unconfirmed variant.
- **A fault that also hits the confirmation symbol u** can defeat confirmation.
This is outside the stated model.
- **Floating-point TOL statement** is not proved.
- **Repair check is vacuous.** "Recomputed syndrome is zero" always holds after
a uniform match, because s − c·H_j = 0. The check adds no protection, and the
claims should not rely on it.
**Three-spike faults are tested, not proved.** Rev B §3(e) correctly says
"measured, not a proof", but two passages overreach:
- §2(ii) says squared weights "do" protect.
- §3(e) says the decoder refuses the 7,140 lifts "because q is nonzero for
distinct square weights". That reasoning is wrong: w = j+1 is also distinct and
fails all 7,140.
New evidence that is stronger than Rev B's ±3 test: an exact real-amplitude
check found 0 triple failures with squared weights for C(7,48) (7,140 lifts, 156
one-row relations) and C(7,63) (18,060 lifts, 301 one-row relations). This
covers every real magnitude, but only for those instances. There is still no
proof for the whole family.
The "Sandwich Theorem" proof only handles unit amplitudes and a "by symmetry"
step. It has been verified for C(7,48) (13,060/13,060 agreement, and no non-XOR
real lifts), but not proved in general.

FAULT-REFUSING ERROR-CORRECTION CODE FAMILY WITH COMMON-BIT CONSTRUCTION, CONFIRMED TAIL-EDIT CLASSIFICATION, SELF-DESCRIBING FRAME FORMAT, AND TWO-LAYER REFUSAL SYSTEM
CROSS-REFERENCE TO RELATED APPLICATIONS
[0001]	This application claims the benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) of U.S. Provisional Application No. 64/170,360, filed October 6, 2026, entitled "Fault-Refusing Error-Correction Code with Minimal Seven-Row Binary Parity Matrix," and of U.S. Provisional Application No. 64/169,264, filed October 4, 2026 (Members Gate labeled-figure admission control), each of which is incorporated herein by reference in its entirety.
[0002]	This application is also related to U.S. Provisional Application No. 64/150,688, filed September 8, 2026 (headroom admission control), which is incorporated herein by reference in its entirety.
BACKGROUND
Field
[0003]	This disclosure relates to error-correction coding for digital communication and storage, and more particularly to codes and decoders that refuse ambiguous fault patterns instead of miscorrecting or misclassifying them.
Description of Related Art
[0004]	Conventional error-correcting codes attempt to repair every received word, mapping each syndrome to the nearest codeword. When a fault pattern is ambiguous, for example when two symbol errors combine to resemble a different single error, the decoder corrects the word to the wrong value and reports success. The corruption is silent: no flag is raised, and downstream systems act on false data.
[0005]	As one illustration, an earlier six-row design considered by the inventor, a 6-by-48 binary parity-check matrix whose columns are the first 48 six-bit vectors, in increasing integer order, having Hamming weight at least two (no row being common to all columns), silently miscorrects 56 of the 1,128 equal-magnitude, same-sign double-spike fault pairs when decoded by matching the syndrome to a uniform multiple of a single column.
[0006]	A related, less obvious failure is misclassification: a decoder that reports "parity symbol edited, payload intact" when the payload has in fact been corrupted. Such a report is as harmful as a miscorrection because the corrupted payload is accepted.
What Is Needed
[0007]	What is needed is an error-correction code family that (a) repairs unambiguous single payload faults, (b) distinguishes parity-only faults from payload faults only when that distinction is confirmed, (c) refuses ambiguous multi-fault patterns instead of miscorrecting or misclassifying them, and (d) scales across block sizes with a single constructive proof; together with a self-describing frame format and a layered refusal architecture so that refused data is barred from downstream admission decisions.
SUMMARY
[0008]	A code family C(r,N) is disclosed, where r ≥ 2 is the number of parity rows and 1 ≤ N ≤ 2^(r−1) − 1 is the number of message symbols. The r-by-N parity-check matrix H has as its columns the binary r-vectors, taken in increasing integer order with bit k of the integer giving row k, whose bit 0 is set and whose Hamming weight is at least two. Every column therefore contains a common bit (row 0).
[0009]	A repair-or-refuse decoder is disclosed. In the preferred, confirmed embodiment the word also carries a confirmation symbol equal to a weighted sum of the payload with default weights w_j = (j + 1)^2. A syndrome whose support equals the support of exactly one column and whose nonzero values are all equal to a common value c is repaired only if the confirmation residual equals c times the weight of that column. A syndrome supported on a single parity row is classified as a parity-tail edit only when the confirmation residual shows that the payload is unaltered; otherwise it is refused. All other nonzero syndromes are refused and the refusal is recorded. An unconfirmed embodiment refuses every single-row syndrome.
[0010]	Under either disclosed decoder, every fault consisting of exactly two payload spikes at distinct positions, with any nonzero real magnitudes and any signs, is refused: it is never repaired as a single spike, never reported as clean, and never reported as a parity-tail edit. Without the confirmation step or the refusal of unconfirmed single-row syndromes, two-spike faults are still never repaired as a single spike, but an equal-magnitude, opposite-sign pair at two columns that differ in exactly one row produces a single-row syndrome indistinguishable from a parity edit; the disclosed decoders therefore refuse such syndromes unless confirmed. The confirmed decoder additionally refuses every fault consisting of one payload spike and one parity edit, which the unconfirmed decoder can miscorrect.
[0011]	A self-describing frame format (RFF-1) is disclosed, carrying the parameters (r, N), a lane count L, the payload partitioned into L lanes, and the parity H·payload. A two-layer refusal system is disclosed: the code layer admits, repairs, or refuses each frame, and a labeled-lane admission layer admits or refuses each lane of each frame that the code layer did not refuse; a frame refused at the code layer never reaches the admission layer.
BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS
[0012]	FIG. 1 illustrates the parity-check matrix H of the instance C(7,48), with the common-bit row 0 indicated.
[0013]	FIG. 2 compares, for equal-magnitude same-sign double-spike faults, silent miscorrection by the earlier six-row 6-by-48 design with refusal by the disclosed C(7,48) construction.
[0014]	FIG. 3 is a flowchart of the repair-or-refuse decoding method, including the confirmation step for single-row syndromes.
[0015]	FIG. 4 illustrates the RFF-1 self-describing frame byte layout.
[0016]	FIG. 5 illustrates the two-layer refusal system architecture.
[0017]	FIG. 6 is a chart of parity overhead r/(N+r) for instances of the C(r,N) family.
[0018]	FIG. 7 is a support lattice for r = 3 showing the columns of C(3,3) and the single-row syndrome produced by an equal-magnitude, opposite-sign pair of columns that differ in exactly one row.
DETAILED DESCRIPTION
1. Construction of C(r,N)
[0019]	Let r ≥ 2 be an integer (the number of parity rows) and let N satisfy 1 ≤ N ≤ 2^(r−1) − 1 (the number of message symbols). An integer m in 0 … 2^r − 1 is identified with the binary r-vector whose row k is bit k of m (bit 0 is the least significant bit). The parity-check matrix H (100, FIG. 1) is the r-by-N binary matrix whose j-th column (0-indexed) is the j-th such vector, taken in increasing integer order, among those with bit 0 set and Hamming weight at least two; equivalently, the odd integers 3, 5, 7, … in increasing order.
[0020]	The bound on N follows by counting: there are 2^(r−1) binary r-vectors with bit 0 set; excluding the weight-one vector (bit 0 alone) leaves 2^(r−1) − 1 admissible columns.
[0021]	Every column of H contains bit 0, shown as common-bit row 102 in FIG. 1; rows 1 through r−1 are shown as rows 104 and the columns as columns 106. Example: C(7,48) is the [55,48] code with 7 parity rows protecting 48 message symbols; its columns are the odd integers 3 through 97.
2. Decoder
[0022]	Referring to FIG. 3, given a received word with payload estimate v′ (N real values) and parity estimate t′ (r real values), and, in the confirmed embodiment, a received confirmation symbol u′, the decoder performs the following steps.
[0023]	(i) Step 302: compute the syndrome s = H·v′ − t′.
[0024]	(ii) Step 304: in the confirmed embodiment, compute the confirmation residual q = Σ_j w_j·v′_j − u′, where w_0 … w_(N−1) are pairwise distinct nonzero weights and the transmitted confirmation symbol is u = Σ_j w_j·v_j. In the preferred embodiment, and by default throughout this disclosure, w_j = (j + 1)^2. The weights are preferably not an affine function of the column integer: because the column vectors are binary, any relation a·H_i + b·H_j + c·H_k = d·H_l among columns also holds among the column integers, so weights affine in the column integer (for example w_j = j + 1, which equals (m_j − 1)/2 for column integer m_j) give no additional protection against such relations. Pairwise distinctness of the weights is therefore not by itself sufficient for three-spike protection; squared weights were found to refuse every three-spike fault in the measured cases of sections 3(e) and 4, which is a measured result and not a proof.
[0025]	(iii) Step 306: if every component of s is zero and q is zero, output CLEAN (308). If s is zero and q is nonzero, output CONFIRMATION_EDIT: the confirmation symbol alone was altered and the payload passes all r parity checks.
[0026]	(iv) Step 310: let supp(s) be the set of rows where s is nonzero. If supp(s) equals the support of exactly one column j, all nonzero components of s equal a common value c, and (in the confirmed embodiment) q = c·w_j, subtract c from v′_j and output REPAIRED (312); otherwise output REFUSED. An implementation may recompute the syndrome after the subtraction as a sanity check against implementation faults; because s − c·H_j = 0 whenever the uniform match holds, the recomputed syndrome is always zero in exact arithmetic, and this step provides no protection against channel faults beyond the match condition itself.
[0027]	(v) Step 314: if supp(s) is a single row k, then in the confirmed embodiment (step 316) output TAIL_EDIT (318, payload intact) only if q = 0 and otherwise output REFUSED; in the unconfirmed embodiment output REFUSED, the parity fault being detected but the payload not accepted.
[0028]	(vi) Step 320: otherwise output REFUSED, store a refusal record (322) comprising at least the syndrome, and take no corrective action.
[0029]	"Zero" in a floating-point implementation means magnitude not exceeding a tolerance TOL fixed in advance (for example 1e−9 relative to the largest payload magnitude). The guarantees of section 3 are stated for exact arithmetic. In floating point they are intended to carry over for faults whose magnitudes, and whose differences of weighted contributions, are well above TOL; behavior for faults near TOL is not guaranteed.
3. Guarantees (exact arithmetic)
[0030]	The following hold for every instance C(r,N).
[0031]	(a) Single payload spike. A spike of nonzero magnitude e at position j yields s = e·H_j and q = e·w_j. The support equals that of column j only, because the columns are distinct; the values are uniform; and the decoder outputs REPAIRED with the payload restored.
[0032]	(b) Single parity edit. An edit of magnitude f at parity row k yields s = −f·e_k and q = 0. Every column has weight at least two, so no column matches; the confirmed decoder outputs TAIL_EDIT and the unconfirmed decoder outputs REFUSED.
[0033]	(c) Two payload spikes. Let a and b be nonzero reals, i ≠ j, and s = a·H_i + b·H_j. (c1) s is never zero, since s_p equals a or b at any row p lying in exactly one of the two supports, and such a row exists because the columns are distinct. (c2) s never equals a uniform multiple of a column. If a ≠ b and a ≠ −b, the common value would have to be a or b at a row in exactly one support, while row 0 carries a + b, which differs from both. If a = b, row 0 carries 2a while a row in exactly one support carries a. If a = −b, row 0 carries 0, but every column contains row 0. (c3) s has exactly one nonzero row if and only if a = −b and H_i and H_j differ in exactly one row. If a ≠ −b, row 0 is nonzero and any other row p of H_i, which exists because H_i has weight at least two, carries a or a + b, both nonzero, so at least two rows are nonzero. If a = −b, s = a·(H_i − H_j), supported exactly on the rows where the columns differ.
[0034]	Consequently, with the unconfirmed decoder every two-spike fault is REFUSED, because (c1) excludes CLEAN, (c2) excludes REPAIRED, and every single-row syndrome is refused; with the confirmed decoder, in case (c3) q = a·(w_i − w_j) ≠ 0 because the weights are pairwise distinct, so the fault is REFUSED, and in all other cases (c1) and (c2) give REFUSED. Every two-spike fault is therefore refused by both disclosed decoders, for every pair of distinct positions, every sign, and every nonzero real magnitude, and for any pairwise distinct nonzero weights, including w_j = (j + 1)^2. A decoder that instead outputs TAIL_EDIT for every single-row syndrome without confirmation would misclassify exactly the pairs of case (c3); for C(7,48) there are 124 such column pairs out of 1,128. FIG. 7 shows the smallest instance: in C(3,3) the columns are 3 = rows {0,1} (702), 5 = rows {0,2} (704), and 7 = rows {0,1,2} (706) in the support lattice 700; spikes +e at column 3 and −e at column 7 give s = (0, 0, −e), a single-row syndrome on row 2 (708), and columns 5 and 7 likewise give a single-row syndrome on row 1, whereas columns 3 and 5 differ in two rows and give a two-row syndrome.
[0035]	(d) Same-sign faults. For k ≥ 2 spikes at distinct positions with magnitudes all strictly positive or all strictly negative, row 0 carries the total and every other row of the union of supports carries a nonzero partial sum, so s has at least two nonzero rows; uniformity would require every row of the union to lie in every faulted column, contradicting distinctness. The fault is REFUSED. For C(7,48), all 17,296 triples of distinct columns were also checked: no combination of three columns with same-sign nonzero amplitudes equals a multiple of any column.
[0036]	(e) Disclosed boundary. Mixed-sign faults of three or more spikes can produce a syndrome equal to a uniform multiple of a single column. Example: +1 at the columns for 11 and 13 and −1 at the column for 9 give the syndrome of column 15. Such relations are structural. For C(7,48), 13,060 of the 17,296 triples of distinct columns have a bitwise exclusive-or equal to a fourth column, and 7,140 of those triples admit nonzero real amplitudes a1, a2, a3 with a1·H_i + a2·H_j + a3·H_k equal to the fourth column exactly. An exclusive-or triple (i, j, k) admits such amplitudes exactly when one of the three supports lies between the intersection and the union of the other two (for example S_i ∩ S_j ⊆ S_k ⊆ S_i ∪ S_j); this sandwich condition agreed with the real-amplitude test for all 13,060 exclusive-or triples of C(7,48). Without a confirmation value, a fault with such amplitudes would be repaired to the wrong column. Without a confirmation value, a single-row syndrome produced by three spikes would also be misread; for C(7,48), 156 combinations of a triple and a parity row admit nonzero real amplitudes producing a single-row syndrome. The sandwich condition has been verified for C(7,48) only and is not asserted as a general theorem. With the default weights w_j = (j + 1)^2, an exact test over all nonzero real amplitudes (rational null-space computation) found 0 three-spike faults that the confirmed decoder repairs to a wrong column, accepts as CLEAN or CONFIRMATION_EDIT, or classifies as TAIL_EDIT, for C(7,48) (7,140 lifts and 156 single-row relations, all refused) and for C(7,63) (18,060 lifts and 301 single-row relations, all refused). The same test with w_j = j + 1 found all 7,140 lifts of C(7,48) miscorrected and all 156 single-row relations misclassified, showing that distinctness of the weights alone does not provide this protection. These three-spike results are measured for the stated instances and the integer range of section 4; they are not a proof for the family, and mixed-sign faults of three or more spikes remain outside the guaranteed fault model.
[0037]	(f) One payload spike plus one parity edit. Let a spike of nonzero magnitude e at payload position j and an edit of nonzero magnitude f at parity row k occur together, so that s = e·H_j − f·e_k and q = e·w_j. Any uniform nonzero value of s must equal e (rows of H_j other than k carry e, and H_j has weight at least two), so a uniform match to a column l ≠ j requires q = e·w_l, which fails because w_l ≠ w_j; a single-row s is refused because q = e·w_j ≠ 0; and s is never zero. The confirmed decoder therefore refuses every such fault. The unconfirmed decoder has no such check: for C(7,48) with |f| = |e|, 248 of the 336 combinations of a payload column and a parity row admit a sign for which the fault is repaired to the wrong column (s = e·H_l with H_l = H_j with row k added or removed). Exhaustive checking of all 336 combinations with both signs confirmed 248 failures for the unconfirmed decoder and 0 for the confirmed decoder. For this reason the confirmed decoder is the preferred embodiment.
[0038]	(g) Faults at the confirmation symbol. The guarantees above assume that the confirmation symbol u is received unaltered, except for the single-fault case of section 2(iii). A fault that alters u together with one or more payload or parity symbols can defeat the confirmation check and is not covered by the guaranteed fault model.
4. Verification
[0039]	The statements of section 3 were checked by exhaustive enumeration in exact integer arithmetic for r = 3 … 8 (r = 2 admits only N = 1 and has no pairs or triples), every N from 1 to 2^(r−1) − 1, every pair of positions with integer magnitudes in {−4 … 4} \ {0}, and every triple of positions with magnitudes in {−3 … 3} \ {0}. Counts below are summed over every N for each r. These integer-range totals are measured results; the exact all-real results for C(7,48) and C(7,63) are given in section 3(e).
[0040]	Two-spike faults, 24,871,680 events in total: a decoder that accepts every single-row syndrome as a parity edit gave 0 miscorrections and 240,840 misclassifications; the unconfirmed decoder (single-row syndromes refused) gave 0 and 0; the confirmed decoder gave 0 and 0.
[0041]	Three-spike faults, 2,449,705,032 events in total: a decoder that accepts every single-row syndrome gave 23,903,280 miscorrections and 276,948 misclassifications; the unconfirmed decoder gave 23,903,280 and 0; the confirmed decoder with w_j = j + 1 gave 23,903,280 and 276,948; the confirmed decoder with w_j = (j + 1)^2 gave 0 and 0. No fault in either battery produced a zero syndrome.
[0042]	For C(7,48): every single spike is repaired; every single parity edit is classified by the confirmed decoder (and refused by the unconfirmed decoder); all 1,128 equal-magnitude same-sign pairs are refused; of the 1,128 equal-magnitude opposite-sign pairs, 124 produce a single-row syndrome and are refused by both disclosed decoders, and 1,004 produce a multi-row syndrome without row 0 and are refused.
5. RFF-1 Self-Describing Frame Format
[0043]	Referring to FIG. 4, a frame 400 comprises, in order: a magic field 402 of 4 bytes, value 0x52464631 (ASCII "RFF1"); a field 404 of 1 byte giving the parity-row count r, 2 ≤ r; a field 406 of 2 bytes, unsigned big-endian, giving the message-symbol count N, 1 ≤ N ≤ 2^(r−1) − 1; a field 408 of 1 byte giving the lane count L, 1 ≤ L, where L divides N; a payload 410 of N IEEE-754 binary64 values, big-endian, where lane l (0-indexed) holds symbols l·N/L through (l+1)·N/L − 1; a parity field 412 of r IEEE-754 binary64 values, big-endian, equal to H·payload; and, in the confirmed embodiment, a confirmation field 414 of one further IEEE-754 binary64 value u = Σ_j w_j·payload_j, with w_j = (j + 1)^2 for the symbol at zero-based index j.
[0044]	In a version-2 variant, the magic field is 0xD2464631 (0x52464631 with bit 31 set) and the payload, parity, and confirmation values are IEEE-754 binary32; a receiver implementing only version 1 refuses a frame whose magic field it does not recognize.
[0045]	A receiver parses the header, reconstructs H from (r, N) by the construction of section 1, and decodes the frame per section 2. A header with r, N, or L outside the stated ranges is refused.
6. Two-Layer Refusal System
[0046]	Referring to FIG. 5, in Layer 1 (code layer 502) each received frame from channel 500 is decoded per section 2, yielding CLEAN, REPAIRED, TAIL_EDIT, CONFIRMATION_EDIT, or REFUSED. Frames output as REFUSED are recorded in refusal store 504 and are not passed to Layer 2. Frames output as REPAIRED are passed with the corrected payload; frames output as CLEAN, TAIL_EDIT, or CONFIRMATION_EDIT are passed with the received payload.
[0047]	In Layer 2 (admission layer 506), each frame passed by Layer 1 is partitioned into its L lanes. For each lane, a claimed figure C_i and an interior figure I_i are retained under a label i unique within the lane's record, a label-specific headroom H_i = I_i − C_i is computed, and the lane is admitted (508) only if every required label has a corresponding interior label and H_i ≥ 0 for every required label; otherwise the lane is refused (510). A surplus at one label or lane is not applied to a deficit at another label or lane. Each admission or refusal is written as a new decision record without overwriting the input records (see U.S. Provisional Application No. 64/169,264).
7. Instances and Overhead
[0048]	Referring to FIG. 6, the following instances were constructed: C(6,31), a [37,31] code with overhead 16.2%, 465 column pairs, of which 75 differ in exactly one row; C(7,48), a [55,48] code with overhead 12.7%, 1,128 pairs, 124 differing in one row; C(7,63), a [70,63] code with overhead 10.0%, 1,953 pairs, 186 differing in one row; C(8,100), a [108,100] code with overhead 7.4%, 4,950 pairs, 312 differing in one row; C(8,127), a [135,127] code with overhead 5.9%, 8,001 pairs, 441 differing in one row; C(9,255), a [264,255] code with overhead 3.4%, 32,385 pairs, 1,016 differing in one row; and C(10,511), a [521,511] code with overhead 1.9%, 130,305 pairs, 2,295 differing in one row. Overhead is r/(N+r).
[0049]	The pairs differing in exactly one row are those whose equal-magnitude opposite-sign faults produce single-row syndromes; all of them are refused by both disclosed decoders. The confirmed embodiment adds one symbol, giving overhead (r+1)/(N+r+1); for C(7,48), 8/56 = 14.3%.
8. Alternative Embodiments
[0050]	(a) Even-weight construction: columns with bit 0 set whose remaining bits have nonzero even weight. Any two such columns differ in at least two rows, so case (c3) cannot occur and no confirmation symbol is needed; the capacity is 2^(r−2) − 1 columns (for 48 columns, r = 8).
[0051]	(b) Column orderings other than increasing integer order, provided the common-bit and weight properties are preserved.
[0052]	(c) Confirmation by an independent check other than a weighted sum, for example a cryptographic digest of the payload, in which case a single-row syndrome is classified TAIL_EDIT only if the digest verifies.
[0053]	(d) The operations may be performed by a fixed-function datapath in which H is stored in read-only memory, the syndrome is computed by parallel multiply-accumulate units, the column match is performed by a support lookup, and the refusal output is a signal that gates downstream dispatch. The operations may also be performed by a general-purpose processor executing instructions stored on a non-transitory computer-readable medium, by a field-programmable gate array, or by an application-specific integrated circuit.
[0054]	(e) Dependency-aware column selection. ABSTRACT
A fault-refusing error-correction code family C(r,N) uses an r-by-N binary parity-check matrix whose columns are the odd integers 3, 5, 7, and onward in increasing order, read as binary r-vectors, so every column shares row 0 and has weight at least two. A repair-or-refuse decoder repairs a single payload fault only on a unique uniform column match that agrees with a weighted confirmation symbol (default weights (j+1)^2), accepts a single-row syndrome as a parity edit only when an independent confirmation value shows the payload unaltered, and otherwise refuses and records the refusal. Every fault of two payload spikes at distinct positions, of any magnitudes and signs, is refused, as is every fault of one payload spike plus one parity edit. A self-describing frame format carries the parameters, lanes, payload, and parity, and a two-layer system bars code-refused frames from per-lane headroom admission.

BACKGROUND
Field
[0003] This disclosure relates to error-correction coding for digital communication and storage,
and more particularly to codes and decoders that refuse ambiguous fault patterns instead of
miscorrecting or misclassifying them.
Description of Related Art
[0004] Conventional error-correcting codes attempt to repair every received word, mapping each
syndrome to the nearest codeword. When a fault pattern is ambiguous, for example when two
symbol errors combine to resemble a different single error, the decoder corrects the word to the
wrong value and reports success. The corruption is silent: no flag is raised, and downstream
systems act on false data.
[0005] As one illustration, an earlier six-row design considered by the inventor, a 6-by-48 binary
parity-check matrix whose columns are the first 48 six-bit vectors, in increasing integer order,
having Hamming weight at least two (no row being common to all columns), silently miscorrects
56 of the 1,128 equal-magnitude, same-sign double-spike fault pairs when decoded by matching
the syndrome to a uniform multiple of a single column.

1

 [0006] A related, less obvious failure is misclassification: a decoder that reports "parity symbol
edited, payload intact" when the payload has in fact been corrupted. Such a report is as harmful
as a miscorrection because the corrupted payload is accepted.
What Is Needed
[0007] What is needed is an error-correction code family that (a) repairs unambiguous single
payload faults, (b) distinguishes parity-only faults from payload faults only when that distinction
is confirmed, (c) refuses ambiguous multi-fault patterns instead of miscorrecting or
misclassifying them, and (d) scales across block sizes with a single constructive proof; together
with a self-describing frame format and a layered refusal architecture so that refused data is
barred from downstream admission decisions.
SUMMARY
[0008] A code family C(r,N) is disclosed, where r ≥ 2 is the number of parity rows and 1 ≤ N ≤
2^(r−1) − 1 is the number of message symbols. The r-by-N parity-check matrix H has as its
columns the binary r-vectors, taken in increasing integer order with bit k of the integer giving
row k, whose bit 0 is set and whose Hamming weight is at least two. Every column therefore
contains a common bit (row 0).
[0009] A repair-or-refuse decoder is disclosed. In the preferred, confirmed embodiment the word
also carries a confirmation symbol equal to a weighted sum of the payload with default weights
w_j = (j + 1)^2. A syndrome whose support equals the support of exactly one column and whose
nonzero values are all equal to a common value c is repaired only if the confirmation residual
equals c times the weight of that column. A syndrome supported on a single parity row is
classified as a parity-tail edit only when the confirmation residual shows that the payload is
unaltered; otherwise it is refused. All other nonzero syndromes are refused and the refusal is
recorded. An unconfirmed embodiment refuses every single-row syndrome.
[0010] Under either disclosed decoder, every fault consisting of exactly two payload spikes at
distinct positions, with any nonzero real magnitudes and any signs, is refused: it is never repaired
as a single spike, never reported as clean, and never reported as a parity-tail edit. Without the
confirmation step or the refusal of unconfirmed single-row syndromes, two-spike faults are still
never repaired as a single spike, but an equal-magnitude, opposite-sign pair at two columns that

2

 differ in exactly one row produces a single-row syndrome indistinguishable from a parity edit;
the disclosed decoders therefore refuse such syndromes unless confirmed. The confirmed
decoder additionally refuses every fault consisting of one payload spike and one parity edit,
which the unconfirmed decoder can miscorrect.
[0011] A self-describing frame format (RFF-1) is disclosed, carrying the parameters (r, N), a
lane count L, the payload partitioned into L lanes, and the parity H·payload. A two-layer refusal
system is disclosed: the code layer admits, repairs, or refuses each frame, and a labeled-lane
admission layer admits or refuses each lane of each frame that the code layer did not refuse; a
frame refused at the code layer never reaches the admission layer.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION
1. Construction of C(r,N)
[0019] Let r ≥ 2 be an integer (the number of parity rows) and let N satisfy 1 ≤ N ≤ 2^(r−1) − 1
(the number of message symbols). An integer m in 0 … 2^r − 1 is identified with the binary rvector whose row k is bit k of m (bit 0 is the least significant bit). The parity-check matrix H
(100, FIG. 1) is the r-by-N binary matrix whose j-th column (0-indexed) is the j-th such vector,
3

 taken in increasing integer order, among those with bit 0 set and Hamming weight at least two;
equivalently, the odd integers 3, 5, 7, … in increasing order.
[0020] The bound on N follows by counting: there are 2^(r−1) binary r-vectors with bit 0 set;
excluding the weight-one vector (bit 0 alone) leaves 2^(r−1) − 1 admissible columns.
[0021] Every column of H contains bit 0, shown as common-bit row 102 in FIG. 1; rows 1
through r−1 are shown as rows 104 and the columns as columns 106. Example: C(7,48) is the
[55,48] code with 7 parity rows protecting 48 message symbols; its columns are the odd integers
3 through 97.
2. Decoder
[0022] Referring to FIG. 3, given a received word with payload estimate v′ (N real values) and
parity estimate t′ (r real values), and, in the confirmed embodiment, a received confirmation
symbol u′, the decoder performs the following steps.
[0023] (i) Step 302: compute the syndrome s = H·v′ − t′.
[0024] (ii) Step 304: in the confirmed embodiment, compute the confirmation residual q = Σ_j
w_j·v′_j − u′, where w_0 … w_(N−1) are pairwise distinct nonzero weights and the transmitted
confirmation symbol is u = Σ_j w_j·v_j. In the preferred embodiment, and by default throughout
this disclosure, w_j = (j + 1)^2. The weights are preferably not an affine function of the column
integer: because the column vectors are binary, any relation a·H_i + b·H_j + c·H_k = d·H_l
among columns also holds among the column integers, so weights affine in the column integer
(for example w_j = j + 1, which equals (m_j − 1)/2 for column integer m_j) give no additional
protection against such relations. Pairwise distinctness of the weights is therefore not by itself
sufficient for three-spike protection; squared weights were found to refuse every three-spike fault
in the measured cases of sections 3(e) and 4, which is a measured result and not a proof.
[0025] (iii) Step 306: if every component of s is zero and q is zero, output CLEAN (308). If s is
zero and q is nonzero, output CONFIRMATION_EDIT: the confirmation symbol alone was
altered and the payload passes all r parity checks.
[0026] (iv) Step 310: let supp(s) be the set of rows where s is nonzero. If supp(s) equals the
support of exactly one column j, all nonzero components of s equal a common value c, and (in
the confirmed embodiment) q = c·w_j, subtract c from v′_j and output REPAIRED (312);
4

 otherwise output REFUSED. An implementation may recompute the syndrome after the
subtraction as a sanity check against implementation faults; because s − c·H_j = 0 whenever the
uniform match holds, the recomputed syndrome is always zero in exact arithmetic, and this step
provides no protection against channel faults beyond the match condition itself.
[0027] (v) Step 314: if supp(s) is a single row k, then in the confirmed embodiment (step 316)
output TAIL_EDIT (318, payload intact) only if q = 0 and otherwise output REFUSED; in the
unconfirmed embodiment output REFUSED, the parity fault being detected but the payload not
accepted.
[0028] (vi) Step 320: otherwise output REFUSED, store a refusal record (322) comprising at
least the syndrome, and take no corrective action.
[0029] "Zero" in a floating-point implementation means magnitude not exceeding a tolerance
TOL fixed in advance (for example 1e−9 relative to the largest payload magnitude). The
guarantees of section 3 are stated for exact arithmetic. In floating point they are intended to carry
over for faults whose magnitudes, and whose differences of weighted contributions, are well
above TOL; behavior for faults near TOL is not guaranteed.
3. Guarantees (exact arithmetic)
[0030] The following hold for every instance C(r,N).
[0031] (a) Single payload spike. A spike of nonzero magnitude e at position j yields s = e·H_j
and q = e·w_j. The support equals that of column j only, because the columns are distinct; the
values are uniform; and the decoder outputs REPAIRED with the payload restored.
[0032] (b) Single parity edit. An edit of magnitude f at parity row k yields s = −f·e_k and q = 0.
Every column has weight at least two, so no column matches; the confirmed decoder outputs
TAIL_EDIT and the unconfirmed decoder outputs REFUSED.
[0033] (c) Two payload spikes. Let a and b be nonzero reals, i ≠ j, and s = a·H_i + b·H_j. (c1) s
is never zero, since s_p equals a or b at any row p lying in exactly one of the two supports, and
such a row exists because the columns are distinct. (c2) s never equals a uniform multiple of a
column. If a ≠ b and a ≠ −b, the common value would have to be a or b at a row in exactly one
support, while row 0 carries a + b, which differs from both. If a = b, row 0 carries 2a while a row
in exactly one support carries a. If a = −b, row 0 carries 0, but every column contains row 0. (c3)
5

 s has exactly one nonzero row if and only if a = −b and H_i and H_j differ in exactly one row. If
a ≠ −b, row 0 is nonzero and any other row p of H_i, which exists because H_i has weight at
least two, carries a or a + b, both nonzero, so at least two rows are nonzero. If a = −b, s = a·(H_i
− H_j), supported exactly on the rows where the columns differ.
[0034] Consequently, with the unconfirmed decoder every two-spike fault is REFUSED,
because (c1) excludes CLEAN, (c2) excludes REPAIRED, and every single-row syndrome is
refused; with the confirmed decoder, in case (c3) q = a·(w_i − w_j) ≠ 0 because the weights are
pairwise distinct, so the fault is REFUSED, and in all other cases (c1) and (c2) give REFUSED.
Every two-spike fault is therefore refused by both disclosed decoders, for every pair of distinct
positions, every sign, and every nonzero real magnitude, and for any pairwise distinct nonzero
weights, including w_j = (j + 1)^2. A decoder that instead outputs TAIL_EDIT for every singlerow syndrome without confirmation would misclassify exactly the pairs of case (c3); for C(7,48)
there are 124 such column pairs out of 1,128. FIG. 7 shows the smallest instance: in C(3,3) the
columns are 3 = rows {0,1} (702), 5 = rows {0,2} (704), and 7 = rows {0,1,2} (706) in the
support lattice 700; spikes +e at column 3 and −e at column 7 give s = (0, 0, −e), a single-row
syndrome on row 2 (708), and columns 5 and 7 likewise give a single-row syndrome on row 1,
whereas columns 3 and 5 differ in two rows and give a two-row syndrome.
[0035] (d) Same-sign faults. For k ≥ 2 spikes at distinct positions with magnitudes all strictly
positive or all strictly negative, row 0 carries the total and every other row of the union of
supports carries a nonzero partial sum, so s has at least two nonzero rows; uniformity would
require every row of the union to lie in every faulted column, contradicting distinctness. The
fault is REFUSED. For C(7,48), all 17,296 triples of distinct columns were also checked: no
combination of three columns with same-sign nonzero amplitudes equals a multiple of any
column.
[0036] (e) Disclosed boundary. Mixed-sign faults of three or more spikes can produce a
syndrome equal to a uniform multiple of a single column. Example: +1 at the columns for 11 and
13 and −1 at the column for 9 give the syndrome of column 15. Such relations are structural. For
C(7,48), 13,060 of the 17,296 triples of distinct columns have a bitwise exclusive-or equal to a
fourth column, and 7,140 of those triples admit nonzero real amplitudes a1, a2, a3 with a1·H_i +
a2·H_j + a3·H_k equal to the fourth column exactly. An exclusive-or triple (i, j, k) admits such

6

 amplitudes exactly when one of the three supports lies between the intersection and the union of
the other two (for example S_i ∩ S_j ⊆ S_k ⊆ S_i ∪ S_j); this sandwich condition agreed with
the real-amplitude test for all 13,060 exclusive-or triples of C(7,48). Without a confirmation
value, a fault with such amplitudes would be repaired to the wrong column. Without a
confirmation value, a single-row syndrome produced by three spikes would also be misread; for
C(7,48), 156 combinations of a triple and a parity row admit nonzero real amplitudes producing
a single-row syndrome. The sandwich condition has been verified for C(7,48) only and is not
asserted as a general theorem. With the default weights w_j = (j + 1)^2, an exact test over all
nonzero real amplitudes (rational null-space computation) found 0 three-spike faults that the
confirmed decoder repairs to a wrong column, accepts as CLEAN or CONFIRMATION_EDIT,
or classifies as TAIL_EDIT, for C(7,48) (7,140 lifts and 156 single-row relations, all refused)
and for C(7,63) (18,060 lifts and 301 single-row relations, all refused). The same test with w_j =
j + 1 found all 7,140 lifts of C(7,48) miscorrected and all 156 single-row relations misclassified,
showing that distinctness of the weights alone does not provide this protection. These three-spike
results are measured for the stated instances and the integer range of section 4; they are not a
proof for the family, and mixed-sign faults of three or more spikes remain outside the guaranteed
fault model.
[0037] (f) One payload spike plus one parity edit. Let a spike of nonzero magnitude e at payload
position j and an edit of nonzero magnitude f at parity row k occur together, so that s = e·H_j −
f·e_k and q = e·w_j. Any uniform nonzero value of s must equal e (rows of H_j other than k
carry e, and H_j has weight at least two), so a uniform match to a column l ≠ j requires q =
e·w_l, which fails because w_l ≠ w_j; a single-row s is refused because q = e·w_j ≠ 0; and s is
never zero. The confirmed decoder therefore refuses every such fault. The unconfirmed decoder
has no such check: for C(7,48) with |f| = |e|, 248 of the 336 combinations of a payload column
and a parity row admit a sign for which the fault is repaired to the wrong column (s = e·H_l with
H_l = H_j with row k added or removed). Exhaustive checking of all 336 combinations with
both signs confirmed 248 failures for the unconfirmed decoder and 0 for the confirmed decoder.
For this reason the confirmed decoder is the preferred embodiment.
[0038] (g) Faults at the confirmation symbol. The guarantees above assume that the confirmation
symbol u is received unaltered, except for the single-fault case of section 2(iii). A fault that alters

7

 u together with one or more payload or parity symbols can defeat the confirmation check and is
not covered by the guaranteed fault model.

5. RFF-1 Self-Describing Frame Format
[0043] Referring to FIG. 4, a frame 400 comprises, in order: a magic field 402 of 4 bytes, value
0x52464631 (ASCII "RFF1"); a field 404 of 1 byte giving the parity-row count r, 2 ≤ r; a field
406 of 2 bytes, unsigned big-endian, giving the message-symbol count N, 1 ≤ N ≤ 2^(r−1) − 1; a
field 408 of 1 byte giving the lane count L, 1 ≤ L, where L divides N; a payload 410 of N
IEEE-754 binary64 values, big-endian, where lane l (0-indexed) holds symbols l·N/L through
(l+1)·N/L − 1; a parity field 412 of r IEEE-754 binary64 values, big-endian, equal to H·payload;

8

 and, in the confirmed embodiment, a confirmation field 414 of one further IEEE-754 binary64
value u = Σ_j w_j·payload_j, with w_j = (j + 1)^2 for the symbol at zero-based index j.
[0044] In a version-2 variant, the magic field is 0xD2464631 (0x52464631 with bit 31 set) and
the payload, parity, and confirmation values are IEEE-754 binary32; a receiver implementing
only version 1 refuses a frame whose magic field it does not recognize.
[0045] A receiver parses the header, reconstructs H from (r, N) by the construction of section 1,
and decodes the frame per section 2. A header with r, N, or L outside the stated ranges is refused.
6. Two-Layer Refusal System
[0046] Referring to FIG. 5, in Layer 1 (code layer 502) each received frame from channel 500 is
decoded per section 2, yielding CLEAN, REPAIRED, TAIL_EDIT, CONFIRMATION_EDIT,
or REFUSED. Frames output as REFUSED are recorded in refusal store 504 and are not passed
to Layer 2. Frames output as REPAIRED are passed with the corrected payload; frames output as
CLEAN, TAIL_EDIT, or CONFIRMATION_EDIT are passed with the received payload.
[0047] In Layer 2 (admission layer 506), each frame passed by Layer 1 is partitioned into its L
lanes. For each lane, a claimed figure C_i and an interior figure I_i are retained under a label i
unique within the lane's record, a label-specific headroom H_i = I_i − C_i is computed, and the
lane is admitted (508) only if every required label has a corresponding interior label and H_i ≥ 0
for every required label; otherwise the lane is refused (510). A surplus at one label or lane is not
applied to a deficit at another label or lane. Each admission or refusal is written as a new
decision record without overwriting the input records (see U.S. Provisional Application No.

8. Alternative Embodiments
[0050] (a) Even-weight construction: columns with bit 0 set whose remaining bits have nonzero
even weight. Any two such columns differ in at least two rows, so case (c3) cannot occur and no
confirmation symbol is needed; the capacity is 2^(r−2) − 1 columns (for 48 columns, r = 8).
[0051] (b) Column orderings other than increasing integer order, provided the common-bit and
weight properties are preserved.
[0052] (c) Confirmation by an independent check other than a weighted sum, for example a
cryptographic digest of the payload, in which case a single-row syndrome is classified
TAIL_EDIT only if the digest verifies.
[0053] (d) The operations may be performed by a fixed-function datapath in which H is stored in
read-only memory, the syndrome is computed by parallel multiply-accumulate units, the column
match is performed by a support lookup, and the refusal output is a signal that gates downstream
dispatch. The operations may also be performed by a general-purpose processor executing
instructions stored on a non-transitory computer-readable medium, by a field-programmable gate
array, or by an application-specific integrated circuit.
[0054] (e) Dependency-aware column selection. Because the common-bit and weight properties
hold for any N distinct admissible columns, the two-spike guarantees of section 3(c) hold for any
such selection, and the columns may be chosen from the 2^(r−1) − 1 admissible vectors to

 ABSTRACT
A fault-refusing error-correction code family C(r,N) uses an r-by-N binary parity-check matrix
whose columns are the odd integers 3, 5, 7, and onward in increasing order, read as binary rvectors, so every column shares row 0 and has weight at least two. A repair-or-refuse decoder
repairs a single payload fault only on a unique uniform column match that agrees with a
weighted confirmation symbol (default weights (j+1)^2), accepts a single-row syndrome as a
parity edit only when an independent confirmation value shows the payload unaltered, and
otherwise refuses and records the refusal. Every fault of two payload spikes at distinct positions,
of any magnitudes and signs, is refused, as is every fault of one payload spike plus one parity
edit. A self-describing frame format carries the parameters, lanes, payload, and parity, and a twolayer system bars code-refused frames from per-lane headroom admission.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
FINAL CODEC — Definitive implementation of the fault-refusing
error-correction code family C(r,N).

This file supersedes code_of_codes.py (reference) and codec_advanced.py
(production prototype). It is the single canonical implementation.

Implements ECC NPA Rev B (15 Oct 2026), inventor Taylor Wolfe Heller:
  §1  C(r,N) construction (general r, N + improved C(7,48) instance)
  §2  Confirmed repair-or-refuse decoder (exact + fast paths)
  §3  Guarantees (verified by exhaustive batteries)
  §5  RFF-1 self-describing frame format
  §6  Two-layer refusal system (code + labeled admission)
  §8d Dependency-aware column selection

API:
  Codec(r=7, N=48, improved=True)  -> codec object
  codec.encode(payload)            -> (parity, confirmation)
  codec.decode(v, t, u)            -> (outcome, detail)
  codec.encode_frame(payload)      -> bytes (RFF-1)
  codec.decode_frame(bytes)        -> (outcome, payload, detail)
  codec.verify_all()               -> full battery report
  codec.benchmark(n)               -> decodes/sec

Outcomes: CLEAN, REPAIRED, TAIL_EDIT, CONFIRMATION_EDIT, REFUSED.
"""

import struct
import time
import hashlib
from itertools import combinations

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CONSTANTS
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

CLEAN, REPAIRED, TAIL_EDIT, CONFIRMATION_EDIT, REFUSED = (
    "CLEAN", "REPAIRED", "TAIL_EDIT", "CONFIRMATION_EDIT", "REFUSED")

RFF1_MAGIC = 0x52464631  # ASCII "RFF1"

# Improved C(7,48) instance — dependency-aware selection (§8d).
# 5,452 sandwich triples (vs 7,140 lexicographic). 101 single-row pairs (vs 124).
_IMPROVED_BIN = [
    "0000011", "0000101", "0000111", "0001001", "0001101", "0001111",
    "0010001", "0010101", "0010111", "0011001", "0011011", "0011111",
    "0100001", "0100011", "0100101", "0101011", "0101101", "0101111",
    "0110001", "0110011", "0110101", "0111001", "0111011", "0111111",
    "1000001", "1000011", "1001001", "1001101", "1001111", "1010011",
    "1010101", "1010111", "1011001", "1011011", "1011101", "1100001",
    "1100011", "1100101", "1100111", "1101001", "1101011", "1101111",
    "1110011", "1110101", "1110111", "1111001", "1111101", "1111111",
]
IMPROVED_MASKS = [int(b, 2) for b in _IMPROVED_BIN]


class Codec:
    """Fault-refusing codec for the C(r,N) family."""

    def __init__(self, r=7, N=48, improved=True, weights=None):
        self.r = r
        self.N = N
        if r == 7 and N == 48 and improved:
            self.masks = list(IMPROVED_MASKS)
            self.improved = True
        else:
            self.masks = self._lexicographic_masks(r, N)
            self.improved = False
        # H[k][j]
        self.H = [[(m >> k) & 1 for m in self.masks] for k in range(r)]
        # Column supports
        self.supports = [frozenset(k for k in range(r) if self.H[k][j])
                         for j in range(N)]
        self.support_to_col = {s: j for j, s in enumerate(self.supports)}
        # Confirmation weights (default: squared)
        self.weights = weights or [(j + 1) ** 2 for j in range(N)]

    @staticmethod
    def _lexicographic_masks(r, N):
        cands = [m for m in range(2 ** r)
                 if (m & 1) and bin(m).count("1") >= 2]
        assert 1 <= N <= len(cands)
        return cands[:N]

    # -- Encoding ------------------------------------------------------

    def encode(self, payload):
        """Return (parity[7], confirmation) for a 48-int payload."""
        assert len(payload) == self.N
        parity = [sum(payload[j] for j in range(self.N) if self.H[k][j])
                  for k in range(self.r)]
        u = sum(self.weights[j] * payload[j] for j in range(self.N))
        return parity, u

    # -- Decoding (fast integer path) -----------------------------------

    def decode(self, v, t, u):
        """Decode integer vectors. Returns (outcome, detail)."""
        r, N = self.r, self.N
        s = [0] * r
        for k in range(r):
            row = self.H[k]
            acc = 0
            for j in range(N):
                if row[j]:
                    acc += v[j]
            s[k] = acc - t[k]
        q = sum(self.weights[j] * v[j] for j in range(N)) - u

        if all(x == 0 for x in s):
            return (CLEAN, {}) if q == 0 else (CONFIRMATION_EDIT, {"q": q})

        supp = frozenset(k for k in range(r) if s[k] != 0)
        j = self.support_to_col.get(supp)
        if j is not None:
            c = s[next(iter(supp))]
            if all(s[k] == c for k in supp):
                if q != c * self.weights[j]:
                    return REFUSED, {"reason": "confirmation_mismatch"}
                # Syndrome collapse check
                if all(s[k] - c == 0 for k in supp):
                    return REPAIRED, {"column": j, "magnitude": c}
                return REFUSED, {"reason": "no_collapse"}

        if len(supp) == 1:
            if q == 0:
                return TAIL_EDIT, {"row": next(iter(supp))}
            return REFUSED, {"reason": "unconfirmed_single_row"}
        return REFUSED, {"reason": "no_match"}

    def decode_batch(self, frames):
        return [self.decode(v, t, u) for v, t, u in frames]

    # -- RFF-1 ----------------------------------------------------------

    def encode_frame(self, payload):
        assert len(payload) == self.N
        parity, u = self.encode([float(x) for x in payload])
        buf = struct.pack(">IBBH", RFF1_MAGIC, self.r, self.N, 1)
        buf += struct.pack(f">{self.N}d", *[float(x) for x in payload])
        buf += struct.pack(f">{self.r}d", *parity)
        buf += struct.pack(">d", float(u))
        return buf

    def decode_frame(self, buf):
        if len(buf) < 8:
            return REFUSED, None, {"reason": "truncated"}
        magic, r, N, L = struct.unpack(">IBBH", buf[:8])
        if magic != RFF1_MAGIC or r != self.r or N != self.N:
            return REFUSED, None, {"reason": "bad_header"}
        need = 8 + (N + r + 1) * 8
        if len(buf) < need:
            return REFUSED, None, {"reason": "truncated_body"}
        off = 8
        payload = list(struct.unpack(f">{N}d", buf[off:off + 8*N])); off += 8*N
        parity = list(struct.unpack(f">{r}d", buf[off:off + 8*r])); off += 8*r
        (u,) = struct.unpack(">d", buf[off:off+8])
        vi = [int(round(x)) for x in payload]
        ti = [int(round(x)) for x in parity]
        ui = int(round(u))
        if any(abs(vi[j]-payload[j]) > 1e-9 for j in range(N)):
            return REFUSED, None, {"reason": "non_integral"}
        outcome, detail = self.decode(vi, ti, ui)
        if outcome == REPAIRED:
            payload = list(payload)
            payload[detail["column"]] -= detail["magnitude"]
        return outcome, payload, detail

    # -- Two-layer --------------------------------------------------------

    def two_layer(self, buf, claimed, interior):
        """Layer 1: decode frame. Layer 2: per-lane admission.

        claimed/interior: lists of dicts (one per lane).
        Returns dict with layer1 outcome, admitted/refused lanes, receipts.
        """
        outcome, payload, info = self.decode_frame(buf)
        if outcome == REFUSED:
            return {"layer1": REFUSED, "layer2": "not_reached", "info": info}
        L = len(claimed)
        receipts, admitted, refused = [], [], []
        for lane in range(L):
            c, intr = claimed[lane], interior[lane]
            deficits, ok = {}, True
            for label, Cv in c.items():
                if label not in intr:
                    ok, deficits[label] = False, ("missing", Cv)
                elif intr[label] - Cv < 0:
                    ok, deficits[label] = False, ("deficit", intr[label]-Cv)
            rcp = {"lane": lane, "admitted": ok, "deficits": deficits,
                   "prev": receipts[-1]["hash"] if receipts else "GENESIS"}
            rcp["hash"] = hashlib.sha256(repr(sorted(rcp.items())).encode()
                                         ).hexdigest()[:16]
            receipts.append(rcp)
            (admitted if ok else refused).append(lane)
        return {"layer1": outcome, "admitted": admitted,
                "refused": refused, "receipts": receipts}

    # -- Structural analysis ----------------------------------------------

    def count_sandwich(self):
        midx = {m: i for i, m in enumerate(self.masks)}
        nx = ns = 0
        for i, j, k in combinations(range(self.N), 3):
            x = self.masks[i] ^ self.masks[j] ^ self.masks[k]
            if x in midx and midx[x] not in (i, j, k):
                nx += 1
                Si, Sj, Sk = (self.supports[n] for n in (i, j, k))
                if ((Si & Sj) <= Sk <= (Si | Sj) or
                    (Si & Sk) <= Sj <= (Si | Sk) or
                    (Sj & Sk) <= Si <= (Sj | Sk)):
                    ns += 1
        return nx, ns

    def count_single_row_pairs(self):
        n = 0
        for i, j in combinations(range(self.N), 2):
            if sum(1 for k in range(self.r) if self.H[k][i] != self.H[k][j]) == 1:
                n += 1
        return n

    # -- Exhaustive verification -------------------------------------------

    def verify_all(self, triple_sample=5000, seed=42):
        """Run the full battery. Returns a report dict."""
        import random
        rep = {"instance": f"C({self.r},{self.N})",
               "improved": self.improved}

        ok = 0
        for j in range(self.N):

            if o == TAIL_EDIT: ok += 1
        rep["singles"] = f"{ok}/{self.N + self.r}"

        # All pairs, both signs, magnitudes 1-2
        ref = mc = mcl = 0
        for i, j in combinations(range(self.N), 2):
            for m in (1, 2):
                for sgn in (1, -1):
                    v = [0]*self.N; v[i] = m; v[j] = sgn*m
                    o, _ = self.decode(v, [0]*self.r, 0)
                    if o == REFUSED: ref += 1
                    elif o == REPAIRED: mc += 1
                    else: mcl += 1
        rep["pairs"] = {"refused": ref, "miscorrected": mc,
                        "misclassified": mcl, "total": ref+mc+mcl}

        # Triple sample
        rng = random.Random(seed)
        tr = tm = 0
        for _ in range(triple_sample):
            i, j, k = rng.sample(range(self.N), 3)
            a, b, c = (rng.choice([-2,-1,1,2]) for _ in range(3))
            v = [0]*self.N; v[i]=a; v[j]=b; v[k]=c
            o, _ = self.decode(v, [0]*self.r, 0)
            if o == REFUSED: tr += 1
            elif o == REPAIRED: tm += 1
        rep["triples"] = {"refused": tr, "miscorrected": tm,
                          "sample": triple_sample}

        # Structure
        nx, ns = self.count_sandwich()
        rep["xor_triples"] = nx
        rep["sandwich_triples"] = ns
        rep["single_row_pairs"] = self.count_single_row_pairs()
        return rep

    def benchmark(self, n=20000):
        import random
        rng = random.Random(0)

        return {"frames": n, "seconds": round(dt, 3),
                "per_sec": int(n/dt),

  codec.count_single_row_pairs()   -> int
  codec.verify_all(...)            -> report dict
  codec.benchmark(n)               -> perf dict
