All integer paths use exact arithmetic. No floating point in decode().
"""

import struct
import time
import hashlib
from itertools import combinations

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CONSTANTS
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

CLEAN, REPAIRED, TAIL_EDIT, CONFIRMATION_EDIT, REFUSED = (
    "CLEAN", "REPAIRED", "TAIL_EDIT", "CONFIRMATION_EDIT", "REFUSED")

RFF1_MAGIC = 0x52464631  # ASCII "RFF1"
RFF1_HEADER_SIZE = 8     # magic(4) + r(1) + N(2) + L(1)

# Improved C(7,48) instance — dependency-aware selection (NPA §8d).
# Binary strings, MSB-first (leftmost char = bit 6, rightmost = bit 0).
# Verified: 5,452 sandwich triples (vs 7,140 lexicographic, -23.6%).
# Verified: 101 single-row pairs (vs 124 lexicographic).
_IMPROVED_BIN = [
    "0000011", "0000101", "0000111", "0001001", "0001101", "0001111",
    "0010001", "0010101", "0010111", "0011001", "0011011", "0011111",
    "0100001", "0100011", "0100101", "0101011", "0101101", "0101111",
    "0110001", "0110011", "0110101", "0111001", "0111011", "0111111",
    "1000001", "1000011", "1001001", "1001101", "1001111", "1010011",
    "1010101", "1010111", "1011001", "1011011", "1011101", "1100001",
    "1100011", "1100101", "1100111", "1101001", "1101011", "1101111",
    "1110011", "1110101", "1110111", "1111001", "1111101", "1111111",
]
IMPROVED_MASKS = [int(b, 2) for b in _IMPROVED_BIN]
assert len(IMPROVED_MASKS) == 48
assert all((m & 1) and bin(m).count("1") >= 2 for m in IMPROVED_MASKS), \
    "improved masks must have bit 0 set and weight >= 2"


class Codec:
    """Fault-refusing codec for the C(r,N) family (NPA §1–§2)."""

    def __init__(self, r=7, N=48, improved=True, weights=None):
        self.r = r
        self.N = N
        if r == 7 and N == 48 and improved:
            self.masks = list(IMPROVED_MASKS)
            self.improved = True
        else:
            self.masks = self._lexicographic_masks(r, N)
            self.improved = False
        # Parity-check matrix H[k][j] (row k, column j)
        self.H = [[(m >> k) & 1 for m in self.masks] for k in range(r)]
        # Column supports as frozensets for O(1) lookup
        self.supports = [frozenset(k for k in range(r) if self.H[k][j])
                         for j in range(N)]
        # Columns are distinct, so support -> column is injective
        assert len(set(self.supports)) == N, "columns must be distinct"
        self.support_to_col = {s: j for j, s in enumerate(self.supports)}
        # Confirmation weights: default w_j = (j+1)^2 (NPA §2(ii))
        self.weights = list(weights) if weights is not None else \
            [(j + 1) ** 2 for j in range(N)]
        assert len(self.weights) == N
        assert len(set(self.weights)) == N, "weights must be pairwise distinct"
        assert all(w != 0 for w in self.weights), "weights must be nonzero"

    @staticmethod
    def _lexicographic_masks(r, N):
        cands = [m for m in range(2 ** r)
                 if (m & 1) and bin(m).count("1") >= 2]
        if not (1 <= N <= len(cands)):
            raise ValueError(f"N={N} out of range for r={r} "
                             f"(max {len(cands)})")
        return cands[:N]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Encoding (NPA §1)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def encode(self, payload):
        """Compute (parity, confirmation) for an integer payload.

        parity[k] = sum_j H[k][j] * payload[j].
        confirmation u = sum_j weights[j] * payload[j].
        """
        if len(payload) != self.N:
            raise ValueError(f"payload length {len(payload)} != N={self.N}")
        parity = [sum(payload[j] for j in range(self.N) if self.H[k][j])
                  for k in range(self.r)]
        u = sum(self.weights[j] * payload[j] for j in range(self.N))
        return parity, u

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Decoding — confirmed repair-or-refuse (NPA §2)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def decode(self, v, t, u):
        """Decode integer vectors (v: payload, t: parity, u: confirmation).

        Returns (outcome, detail_dict). Exact integer arithmetic.
        Implements NPA §2 steps (iii)–(vi).
        """
        r, N = self.r, self.N
        if not (len(v) == N and len(t) == r):
            raise ValueError("vector length mismatch")

        # (ii) Syndrome s = H·v − t; confirmation residual q = Σw·v − u
        s = [sum(v[j] for j in range(N) if self.H[k][j]) - t[k]
             for k in range(r)]
        q = sum(self.weights[j] * v[j] for j in range(N)) - u

        # (iii) Zero syndrome
        if all(x == 0 for x in s):
            if q == 0:
                return CLEAN, {}
            return CONFIRMATION_EDIT, {"q": q}

        supp = frozenset(k for k in range(r) if s[k] != 0)

        # (iv) Unique uniform single-column match
        j = self.support_to_col.get(supp)
        if j is not None:
            c = s[next(iter(supp))]
            if all(s[k] == c for k in supp):
                # Confirmation must match: q == c · w_j
                if q != c * self.weights[j]:
                    return REFUSED, {"reason": "confirmation_mismatch",
                                     "column": j, "q": q,
                                     "expected": c * self.weights[j]}
                # Repair: subtract c from v[j], recompute syndrome,
                # accept only on full collapse to zero
                v2 = list(v)
                v2[j] -= c
                s2 = [sum(v2[jj] for jj in range(N) if self.H[k][jj]) - t[k]
                      for k in range(r)]
                if all(x == 0 for x in s2):
                    return REPAIRED, {"column": j, "magnitude": c}
                return REFUSED, {"reason": "no_syndrome_collapse",
                                 "column": j}

        # (v) Single-row syndrome: TAIL_EDIT only if q == 0
        if len(supp) == 1:
            if q == 0:
                return TAIL_EDIT, {"row": next(iter(supp))}
            return REFUSED, {"reason": "unconfirmed_single_row",
                             "row": next(iter(supp))}

        # (vi) Refuse everything else
        return REFUSED, {"reason": "no_match"}

    def decode_batch(self, frames):
        """Decode an iterable of (v, t, u) tuples."""
        return [self.decode(v, t, u) for v, t, u in frames]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # RFF-1 wire format (NPA §5)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def encode_frame(self, payload, L=1):
        """Encode payload into RFF-1 bytes.

        Layout: magic(4) | r(1) | N(2BE) | L(1) | payload(N f64BE)
                | parity(r f64BE) | confirmation(f64BE).
        L must divide N.
        """
        if len(payload) != self.N:
            raise ValueError(f"payload length {len(payload)} != N={self.N}")
        if not (1 <= L and self.N % L == 0):
            raise ValueError(f"L={L} must divide N={self.N}")
        parity, u = self.encode([float(x) for x in payload])
        buf = struct.pack(">IBBH", RFF1_MAGIC, self.r, self.N, L)
        buf += struct.pack(f">{self.N}d", *[float(x) for x in payload])
        buf += struct.pack(f">{self.r}d", *parity)
        buf += struct.pack(">d", float(u))
        return buf

    def decode_frame(self, buf):
        """Decode RFF-1 bytes. Returns (outcome, payload_or_None, detail).

        Payloads must be integral (within 1e-9) for exact decoding;
        non-integral payloads are refused.
        """
        if len(buf) < RFF1_HEADER_SIZE:
            return REFUSED, None, {"reason": "truncated_header"}
        magic, r, N, L = struct.unpack(">IBBH", buf[:RFF1_HEADER_SIZE])
        if magic != RFF1_MAGIC:
            return REFUSED, None, {"reason": "bad_magic"}
        if r != self.r or N != self.N:
            return REFUSED, None, {"reason": "param_mismatch",
                                   "got": (r, N), "expected": (self.r, self.N)}
        if not (1 <= L and N % L == 0):
            return REFUSED, None, {"reason": "bad_lane_count", "L": L}
        need = RFF1_HEADER_SIZE + (N + r + 1) * 8
        if len(buf) < need:
            return REFUSED, None, {"reason": "truncated_body"}

        off = RFF1_HEADER_SIZE
        payload = list(struct.unpack(f">{N}d", buf[off:off + 8 * N]))
        off += 8 * N
        parity = list(struct.unpack(f">{r}d", buf[off:off + 8 * r]))
        off += 8 * r
        (u,) = struct.unpack(">d", buf[off:off + 8])

        vi = [int(round(x)) for x in payload]
        ti = [int(round(x)) for x in parity]
        ui = int(round(u))
        if any(abs(vi[j] - payload[j]) > 1e-9 for j in range(N)):
            return REFUSED, None, {"reason": "non_integral_payload"}

        outcome, detail = self.decode(vi, ti, ui)
        if outcome == REPAIRED:
            payload = list(payload)
            payload[detail["column"]] -= detail["magnitude"]
        detail["L"] = L
        return outcome, payload, detail

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Two-layer refusal system (NPA §6)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def two_layer(self, buf, claimed, interior):
        """Full pipeline: Layer 1 (code) then Layer 2 (labeled admission).

        claimed/interior: lists of dicts, one per lane; len must match
        the frame's L. Each lane admitted only if every claimed label has
        an interior label and every headroom h_i = I_i − C_i >= 0.
        No cross-label offset. Receipts are hash-chained.
        """
        outcome, payload, info = self.decode_frame(buf)
        if outcome == REFUSED:
            return {"layer1": REFUSED, "layer2": "not_reached", "info": info}
        L = info["L"]
        if not (len(claimed) == L and len(interior) == L):
            raise ValueError(f"claimed/interior length must equal L={L}")
        receipts, admitted, refused = [], [], []
        for lane in range(L):
            c, intr = claimed[lane], interior[lane]
            deficits, ok = {}, True
            for label, Cv in c.items():
                if label not in intr:
                    ok = False
                    deficits[label] = ("missing_interior", Cv)
                else:
                    h = intr[label] - Cv
                    if h < 0:
                        ok = False
                        deficits[label] = ("negative_headroom", h)
            rcp = {"lane": lane, "admitted": ok, "deficits": deficits,
                   "prev": receipts[-1]["hash"] if receipts else "GENESIS"}
            rcp["hash"] = hashlib.sha256(
                repr(sorted(rcp.items())).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
            receipts.append(rcp)
            (admitted if ok else refused).append(lane)
        return {"layer1": outcome, "payload": payload,
                "admitted": admitted, "refused": refused,
                "receipts": receipts}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Structural analysis (NPA §3(e))
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def count_sandwich(self):
        """Count (n_xor, n_sandwich): triples with mask XOR = 4th mask,
        and how many satisfy the sandwich condition (up to permutation)."""
        midx = {m: i for i, m in enumerate(self.masks)}
        nx = ns = 0
        for i, j, k in combinations(range(self.N), 3):
            x = self.masks[i] ^ self.masks[j] ^ self.masks[k]
            t = midx.get(x)
            if t is not None and t not in (i, j, k):
                nx += 1
                Si, Sj, Sk = (self.supports[n] for n in (i, j, k))
                if ((Si & Sj) <= Sk <= (Si | Sj) or
                    (Si & Sk) <= Sj <= (Si | Sk) or
                    (Sj & Sk) <= Si <= (Sj | Sk)):
                    ns += 1
        return nx, ns

    def count_single_row_pairs(self):
        """Count column pairs differing in exactly one row (NPA §3(c3))."""
        n = 0
        for i, j in combinations(range(self.N), 2):
            if sum(1 for k in range(self.r)
                   if self.H[k][i] != self.H[k][j]) == 1:
                n += 1
        return n

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Exhaustive verification (NPA §3–§4)
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    def verify_all(self, triple_sample=5000, seed=42):
        """Run the full battery. Returns a report dict.

        Covers: all singles, all parity edits, confirmation-edit path,
        all pairs (magnitudes 1–3, both signs), triple sample
        (magnitudes −3..3), structural counts.
        """
        import random
        rep = {"instance": f"C({self.r},{self.N})",
               "improved": self.improved}

        # Singles: every position, magnitude 3
        ok = 0
        for j in range(self.N):
            v = [0] * self.N
            v[j] = 3
            o, d = self.decode(v, [0] * self.r, 0)
            if o == REPAIRED and d.get("column") == j:
                ok += 1
        # Parity edits: every row, magnitude 5
        for k in range(self.r):
            t = [0] * self.r
            t[k] = 5
            o, _ = self.decode([0] * self.N, t, 0)
            if o == TAIL_EDIT:
                ok += 1
        rep["singles"] = f"{ok}/{self.N + self.r}"

        # Confirmation-edit: zero syndrome, nonzero q
        o, _ = self.decode([0] * self.N, [0] * self.r, 7)
        rep["confirmation_edit"] = ("OK" if o == CONFIRMATION_EDIT
                                    else f"FAIL({o})")

        # All pairs, magnitudes 1–3, both signs
        ref = mc = mcl = 0
        for i, j in combinations(range(self.N), 2):
            for m in (1, 2, 3):
                for sgn in (1, -1):
                    v = [0] * self.N
                    v[i], v[j] = m, sgn * m
                    o, _ = self.decode(v, [0] * self.r, 0)
                    if o == REFUSED:
                        ref += 1
                    elif o == REPAIRED:
                        mc += 1
                    else:
                        mcl += 1
        rep["pairs"] = {"refused": ref, "miscorrected": mc,
                        "misclassified": mcl, "total": ref + mc + mcl}

        # Triple sample, magnitudes −3..3 excluding 0
        rng = random.Random(seed)
        tr = tm = 0
        for _ in range(triple_sample):
            i, j, k = rng.sample(range(self.N), 3)
            a, b, c = (rng.choice([-3, -2, -1, 1, 2, 3]) for _ in range(3))
            v = [0] * self.N
            v[i], v[j], v[k] = a, b, c
            o, _ = self.decode(v, [0] * self.r, 0)
            if o == REFUSED:
                tr += 1
            elif o == REPAIRED:
                tm += 1
        rep["triples"] = {"refused": tr, "miscorrected": tm,
                          "sample": triple_sample}

        # Structural counts
        nx, ns = self.count_sandwich()
        rep["xor_triples"] = nx
        rep["sandwich_triples"] = ns
        rep["single_row_pairs"] = self.count_single_row_pairs()
        return rep

    def benchmark(self, n=20000):
        """Decode n random single-spike frames; return throughput."""
        import random
        rng = random.Random(0)
        frames = []
        for _ in range(n):
            v = [0] * self.N

            frames.append((v, [0] * self.r, 0))
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        res = self.decode_batch(frames)
        dt = time.perf_counter() - t0
        return {"frames": n, "seconds": round(dt, 3),
                "per_sec": int(n / dt),
                "repaired": sum(1 for o, _ in res if o == REPAIRED)}

BACKGROUND

1. Field. This disclosure relates to error-correction coding for digital communication and storage, and more particularly to codes and decoders that refuse ambiguous fault patterns instead of miscorrecting or misclassifying them.

2. Description of related art. Conventional error-correcting codes attempt to repair every received word, mapping each syndrome to the nearest codeword. When a fault pattern is ambiguous — for example, when two symbol errors combine to resemble a different single error — the decoder "corrects" the word to the wrong value and reports success. The corruption is silent: no flag is raised, and downstream systems act on false data. As one illustration, an earlier six-row design considered by the inventor (a 6-by-48 binary parity matrix whose columns are the first 48 six-bit vectors of Hamming weight at least two) silently miscorrects 56 of the 1,128 equal-magnitude, same-sign double-spike fault pairs. [ATTORNEY: confirm whether this six-row design should be characterized at all, and how; it is the inventor's own earlier design, not a published standard.]

A related, less obvious failure is misclassification: a decoder that reports "parity symbol edited, payload intact" when the payload has in fact been corrupted. Such a report is as harmful as a miscorrection because the corrupted payload is accepted.

3. What is needed. An error-correction code family that (a) repairs unambiguous single payload faults, (b) distinguishes parity-only faults from payload faults only when that distinction is confirmed, (c) refuses ambiguous multi-fault patterns instead of miscorrecting or misclassifying them, and (d) scales across block sizes with a single constructive proof; together with a self-describing frame format and a layered refusal architecture so that refused data is barred from downstream admission decisions.

SUMMARY

A code family C(r,N) is disclosed, where r ≥ 2 is the number of parity rows and 1 ≤ N ≤ 2^(r−1) − 1 is the number of message symbols. The r-by-N parity-check matrix H has as its columns the binary r-vectors, taken in increasing integer order with bit k of the integer giving row k, whose bit 0 is set and whose Hamming weight is at least 2. Every column therefore contains a common bit (row 0).

A repair-or-refuse decoder is disclosed. A syndrome whose support equals the support of exactly one column and whose nonzero values are all equal is repaired, and the repair is accepted only if the recomputed syndrome is zero. A syndrome supported on a single parity row is classified as a parity-tail edit only when an independent confirmation value shows that the payload is unaltered; otherwise it is refused. All other nonzero syndromes are refused and the refusal is recorded.

It is proved that, under this decoder, every fault consisting of exactly two payload spikes at distinct positions, with any nonzero real magnitudes and any signs, is refused: it is never repaired as a single spike, never reported as clean, and never reported as a parity-tail edit. Without the confirmation step, the same two-spike faults are still never repaired as a single spike, but an equal-magnitude, opposite-sign pair at two columns that differ in exactly one row produces a single-row syndrome; the disclosed decoder therefore refuses such syndromes unless confirmed.

A self-describing frame format (RFF-1) is disclosed, carrying the parameters (r, N), a lane count L, the payload partitioned into L lanes, and the parity H·payload. A two-layer refusal system is disclosed: the code layer admits, repairs, or refuses each frame, and a labeled-lane admission layer admits or refuses each lane of each frame that the code layer did not refuse; a frame refused at the code layer never reaches the admission layer.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION

1. Construction of C(r,N)

Let r ≥ 2 be an integer (the number of parity rows) and let N satisfy 1 ≤ N ≤ 2^(r−1) − 1 (the number of message symbols). An integer m in 0 … 2^r − 1 is identified with the binary r-vector whose row k is bit k of m (bit 0 is the least significant bit). The parity-check matrix H is the r-by-N binary matrix whose j-th column (0-indexed) is the j-th such vector, taken in increasing integer order, among those with bit 0 set and Hamming weight at least 2 — equivalently, the odd integers 3, 5, 7, … in increasing order.

The bound on N follows by counting: there are 2^(r−1) binary r-vectors with bit 0 set; excluding the weight-1 vector (bit 0 alone) leaves 2^(r−1) − 1 admissible columns.

Every column of H contains bit 0. Example: C(7,48) is the [55,48] code with 7 parity rows protecting 48 message symbols; its columns are the odd integers 3 through 97.

2. Decoder

Given a received word with payload estimate v′ (N real values) and parity estimate t′ (r real values), and, in the confirmed embodiment, a received confirmation symbol u′, the decoder performs:

(i) Compute the syndrome s = H·v′ − t′.
(ii) In the confirmed embodiment, compute the confirmation residual q = Σ_j w_j·v′_j − u′, where w_0 … w_(N−1) are pairwise distinct nonzero weights and the transmitted confirmation symbol is u = Σ_j w_j·v_j.
In a preferred embodiment w_j = (j + 1)^2. The weights are preferably not an affine function of the column integer: because the column vectors are binary with no carries, any relation a·H_i + b·H_j + c·H_k = d·H_l among columns also holds among the column integers, so weights affine in the column integer (for example w_j = j + 1, which equals (m_j − 1)/2 for column integer m_j) give no additional protection against such relations, whereas squared weights do in the tested range (section 4).
(iii) If every component of s is zero (and q is zero), output CLEAN. If s is zero and q is nonzero, output CONFIRMATION_EDIT (the confirmation symbol alone was altered; the payload passes all r parity checks).
(iv) Let supp(s) be the set of rows where s is nonzero. If supp(s) equals the support of exactly one column j, all nonzero components of s equal a common value c, and (in the confirmed embodiment) q = c·w_j, subtract c from v′_j, recompute the syndrome, and output REPAIRED only if the recomputed syndrome is zero; otherwise output REFUSED.
(v) If supp(s) is a single row k: in the confirmed embodiment output TAIL_EDIT (payload intact) only if q = 0, and otherwise output REFUSED; in the unconfirmed embodiment output REFUSED (the parity fault is detected but the payload is not accepted).
(vi) Otherwise output REFUSED, store a refusal record comprising at least the syndrome, and take no corrective action.

"Zero" in a floating-point implementation means magnitude not exceeding a tolerance TOL fixed in advance (for example 1e−9 relative to the largest payload magnitude); the guarantees of section 3 are stated for exact arithmetic and hold in floating point for faults whose magnitudes, and whose pairwise differences of weighted contributions, exceed TOL.

3. Guarantees (exact arithmetic)

For every instance C(r,N):

(a) Single payload spike. A spike of nonzero magnitude e at position j yields s = e·H_j and q = e·w_j; the support equals that of column j only (columns are distinct), the values are uniform, and the decoder outputs REPAIRED with the payload restored.

(b) Single parity edit. An edit of magnitude f at parity row k yields s = −f·e_k and q = 0. Every column has weight at least 2, so no column matches; the confirmed decoder outputs TAIL_EDIT and the unconfirmed decoder outputs REFUSED.

(c) Two payload spikes. Let a, b be nonzero reals and i ≠ j. Then s = a·H_i + b·H_j and:
 (c1) s is never zero, since s_p = a or b at any row p in exactly one of the two supports, and such a row exists because the columns are distinct.
 (c2) s never matches a column with uniform values. If a ≠ b and a ≠ −b: pick p in one support only, so the common value would be a (or b); row 0 then carries a + b, which differs from both. If a = b: row 0 carries 2a while a row in exactly one support carries a. If a = −b: row 0 carries 0, but every column contains row 0.
 (c3) s has exactly one nonzero row if and only if a = −b and H_i, H_j differ in exactly one row. Proof: if a ≠ −b, row 0 is nonzero, and any other row p of H_i (which exists, weight ≥ 2) carries a or a + b ≠ 0, so at least two rows are nonzero. If a = −b, s = a·(H_i − H_j), supported exactly on the rows where the columns differ.
 Consequently: with the unconfirmed decoder, every two-spike fault is REFUSED; with the confirmed decoder, in case (c3) q = a·(w_i − w_j) ≠ 0, so the fault is REFUSED; in all other cases (c1)–(c2) give REFUSED. Every two-spike fault is therefore refused by both disclosed decoders. A decoder that outputs TAIL_EDIT for every single-row syndrome without confirmation would misclassify exactly the pairs in (c3); for C(7,48) there are 124 such column pairs.

(d) Same-sign faults. For k ≥ 2 spikes at distinct positions with magnitudes all strictly positive or all strictly negative: row 0 carries the total, every other row of the union of supports carries a nonzero partial sum, so s has at least two nonzero rows and is nonzero; and uniformity would require every row of the union to lie in every faulted column, contradicting distinctness. The fault is REFUSED.

(e) Disclosed boundary. Mixed-sign faults of three or more spikes can produce a syndrome equal to a uniform multiple of a single column (example: +1 at the columns for 11 and 13 and −1 at the column for 9 give the syndrome of column 15). With squared weights, the confirmed decoder refused every three-spike fault in the exhaustively tested range (section 4); this is a measured result for that range, not a proof, and three-or-more-spike mixed-sign faults remain outside the guaranteed fault model.

The structure of these collisions is characterized exactly by the Sandwich Theorem. Let i,j,k be distinct column indices whose masks satisfy mask_i XOR mask_j XOR mask_k = mask_t for a fourth column t. Write S_i, S_j, S_k for the supports (sets of rows where the column has a 1). Then nonzero real amplitudes with a1·col_i + a2·col_j + a3·col_k exactly equal to col_t exist if and only if one support is sandwiched between the intersection and union of the other two: (S_i ∩ S_j) ⊆ S_k ⊆ (S_i ∪ S_j), or the corresponding condition with the indices permuted. Proof: for a sign pattern (+,+,-), at each row the bits (b_i,b_j,b_k) must satisfy b_i + b_j − b_k = b_t ∈ {0,1}; the patterns (0,0,1) and (1,1,0) are impossible, and these are exactly the sandwich violations; the other sign patterns follow by symmetry. For C(7,48): 13,060 triples satisfy the XOR condition, of which 7,140 satisfy the sandwich condition and therefore lift to exact real collisions. The confirmed decoder with squared weights refuses these because the confirmation residual q = Σw_j·e_j is nonzero for distinct square weights (section 4); the sandwich characterization explains why the collisions exist and guides column selection (section 8(d)).

4. Verification

The statements of section 3 were checked by exhaustive enumeration in exact integer arithmetic (scripts ecc_verify.py and doc_checks.py) for r = 2 … 8, every N from 1 to 2^(r−1) − 1, every pair of positions with integer magnitudes in {−4 … 4} \ {0}, and every triple of positions with magnitudes in {−3 … 3} \ {0}. Results (counts summed over every N for each r): two-spike faults, 24,871,680 events in total for r = 2 … 8 — decoder as in the 15 Oct draft: 0 miscorrections and 240,840 misclassifications (single-row syndrome reported as a parity edit); unconfirmed decoder (single-row syndromes refused): 0 and 0; confirmed decoder: 0 and 0. Three-spike faults, 2,449,705,032 events in total — decoder as in the 15 Oct draft: 23,903,280 miscorrections and 276,948 misclassifications; unconfirmed decoder: 23,903,280 and 0; confirmed decoder with w_j = j + 1: 23,903,280 and 276,948; confirmed decoder with w_j = (j + 1)^2: 0 and 0. No fault in either battery produced a zero syndrome. For C(7,48): 48 of 48 single spikes repaired; 7 of 7 parity edits classified; 1,128 of 1,128 equal-magnitude same-sign pairs refused; of 1,128 equal-magnitude opposite-sign pairs, 124 produce a single-row syndrome (refused by both disclosed decoders) and 1,004 produce a multi-row syndrome without row 0 (refused).

5. RFF-1 self-describing frame format

A frame comprises, in order:
- magic: 4 bytes, value 0x52464631 (ASCII "RFF1");
- r: 1 byte, the parity-row count, 2 ≤ r;
- N: 2 bytes, unsigned big-endian, the message-symbol count, 1 ≤ N ≤ 2^(r−1) − 1;
- L: 1 byte, the lane count, 1 ≤ L, where L divides N;
- payload: N IEEE-754 binary64 values, big-endian, where lane l (0-indexed) holds symbols l·N/L through (l+1)·N/L − 1;
- parity: r IEEE-754 binary64 values, big-endian, equal to H·payload;
- in the confirmed embodiment, one further IEEE-754 binary64 value u = Σ_j w_j·payload_j, with w_j = j + 1 unless otherwise signaled.

A receiver parses the header, reconstructs H from (r, N) by the construction of section 1, and decodes the frame per section 2. A header with r, N, or L outside the stated ranges is refused.

6. Two-layer refusal system

Layer 1 (code): each received frame is decoded per section 2, yielding CLEAN, REPAIRED, TAIL_EDIT, CONFIRMATION_EDIT, or REFUSED. Frames output as REFUSED are recorded and are not passed to Layer 2. Frames output as REPAIRED are passed with the corrected payload; frames output as CLEAN, TAIL_EDIT, or CONFIRMATION_EDIT are passed with the received payload.

Layer 2 (admission): each frame passed by Layer 1 is partitioned into its L lanes. For each lane, a claimed figure C_i and an interior figure I_i are retained under a label i unique within the lane's record, a label-specific headroom H_i = I_i − C_i is computed, and the lane is admitted only if every required label has a corresponding interior label and H_i ≥ 0 for every required label; otherwise the lane is refused. A surplus at one label or lane is not applied to a deficit at another label or lane. Each admission or refusal is written as a new decision record without overwriting the input records (see U.S. Provisional Application No. 64/169,264, paragraphs [0008]–[0010], [0018]–[0022]).

8. Alternative embodiments

(a) Even-weight construction: columns with bit 0 set whose remaining bits have nonzero even weight; any two such columns differ in at least two rows, so case (c3) cannot occur and no confirmation symbol is needed; capacity is 2^(r−2) − 1 columns (for 48 columns, r = 8). [ATTORNEY: this construction appears in Drive material dated 8 October 2026 marked "new matter"; confirm whether it was filed in a separate provisional.]
(b) Column orderings other than increasing integer order, provided the common-bit and weight properties are preserved.
(c) Confirmation by a second independent check other than a weighted sum (for example a cryptographic digest of the payload), in which case a single-row syndrome is classified TAIL_EDIT only if the digest verifies.

(d) Dependency-aware column selection. In place of the increasing-integer-order selection of section 1, the N columns are chosen from the 2^(r−1)−1 admissible masks (bit 0 set, weight at least 2) to minimize the number of triples satisfying the sandwich condition of section 3(e), via combinatorial optimization. The common-bit property holds for any such selection, so the pair-refusal guarantee of section 3(c) is unchanged. For C(7,48), dependency-aware selection reduces sandwich triples from 7,140 (increasing integer order) to 5,452, a 23.6% reduction. An improved instance uses the 48 masks (binary, bit 0 = LSB): 0000011, 0000101, 0000111, 0001001, 0001101, 0001111, 0010001, 0010101, 0010111, 0011001, 0011011, 0011111, 0100001, 0100011, 0100101, 0101011, 0101101, 0101111, 0110001, 0110011, 0110101, 0111001, 0111011, 0111111, 1000001, 1000011, 1001001, 1001101, 1001111, 1010011, 1010101, 1010111, 1011001, 1011011, 1011101, 1100001, 1100011, 1100101, 1100111, 1101001, 1101011, 1101111, 1110011, 1110101, 1110111, 1111001, 1111101, 1111111.

(e) Soft-decision decoder variant. In place of the exact support/collinearity test of section 2, the decoder computes for each column the projection residual and repairs to the column with residual below a threshold τ, refusing if zero or multiple columns qualify.

(f) Adaptive threshold. The tolerance TOL is set from the measured channel noise floor as TOL = κ·σ with κ ≥ 3, matching refusal rates to channel conditions.

(g) RFF-1 version 2. Bit 31 of the magic field set (0xD2464631) signals 32-bit floats in place of 64-bit, halving frame size; version-1 receivers refuse version-2 frames with a version-mismatch code.

(h) Hardware embodiment. Syndrome computation and column matching as a fixed-function datapath with H in ROM and a single-bit refusal output gating downstream dispatch.

(i) Concatenated embodiment. The C(r,N) code as inner code with an outer Reed-Solomon code treating refused blocks as erasures.

9. Industrial applicability

The family is applicable to any digital link or storage medium where silent data corruption is costlier than retransmission or erasure: radio links, satellite command links, sensor feeds, and autonomous-system sensor buses, among others.

ABSTRACT

A fault-refusing error-correction code family C(r,N) is disclosed. Its r-by-N binary parity-check matrix uses as columns the odd integers 3, 5, 7, … in increasing order, read as binary r-vectors, so every column shares row 0 and has weight at least two. A repair-or-refuse decoder repairs a single payload fault only on a unique uniform column match confirmed by syndrome collapse, accepts a single-row syndrome as a parity edit only when an independent confirmation value shows the payload unaltered, and otherwise refuses and records the refusal. Every fault of two payload spikes at distinct positions, of any magnitudes and signs, is refused. A self-describing frame format carries the parameters, lanes, payload, and parity, and a two-layer system bars code-refused frames from per-lane, per-label headroom admission.

ABSTRACT
A fault-refusing error-correction code family C(r,N) is disclosed. Its r-by-N binary parity-check matrix uses as columns the odd integers 3, 5, 7, … in increasing order, read as binary r-vectors, so every column shares row 0 and has weight at least two. A repair-or-refuse decoder repairs a single payload fault only on a unique uniform column match confirmed by syndrome collapse, accepts a single-row syndrome as a parity edit only when an independent confirmation value shows the payload unaltered, and otherwise refuses and records the refusal. Every fault of two payload spikes at distinct positions, of any magnitudes and signs, is refused. A self-describing frame format carries the parameters, lanes, payload, and parity, and a two-layer system bars code-refused frames from per-lane, per-label headroom admission.

BACKGROUND
1. Field. This disclosure relates to error-correction coding for digital
communication and storage, and more particularly to codes and decoders that
refuse ambiguous fault patterns instead of miscorrecting or misclassifying
them.
2. Description of related art. Conventional error-correcting codes attempt to
repair every received word, mapping each syndrome to the nearest codeword.
When a fault pattern is ambiguous -- for example, when two symbol errors
combine to resemble a different single error -- the decoder "corrects" the
word to the wrong value and reports success. The corruption is silent: no
flag is raised, and downstream systems act on false data. As one
illustration, an earlier six-row design considered by the inventor (a 6-by-48
binary parity matrix whose columns are the first 48 six-bit vectors of
Hamming weight at least two) silently miscorrects 56 of the 1,128
equal-magnitude, same-sign double-spike fault pairs. [ATTORNEY: confirm
whether this six-row design should be characterized at all, and how; it is
the inventor's own earlier design, not a published standard.]
A related, less obvious failure is misclassification: a decoder that reports
"parity symbol edited, payload intact" when the payload has in fact been
corrupted. Such a report is as harmful as a miscorrection because the
corrupted payload is accepted.
3. What is needed. An error-correction code family that (a) repairs
unambiguous single payload faults, (b) distinguishes parity-only faults from
payload faults only when that distinction is confirmed, (c) refuses ambiguous
multi-fault patterns instead of miscorrecting or misclassifying them, and (d)
scales across block sizes with a single constructive proof; together with a
self-describing frame format and a layered refusal architecture so that
refused data is barred from downstream admission decisions.

SUMMARY
A code family C(r,N) is disclosed, where r >= 2 is the number of parity rows
and 1 <= N <= 2^(r-1) - 1 is the number of message symbols. The r-by-N
parity-check matrix H has as its columns the binary r-vectors, taken in
increasing integer order with bit k of the integer giving row k, whose bit 0
is set and whose Hamming weight is at least 2. Every column therefore
contains a common bit (row 0).
A repair-or-refuse decoder is disclosed. A syndrome whose support equals the

 support of exactly one column and whose nonzero values are all equal is
repaired, and the repair is accepted only if the recomputed syndrome is zero.
A syndrome supported on a single parity row is classified as a parity-tail
edit only when an independent confirmation value shows that the payload is
unaltered; otherwise it is refused. All other nonzero syndromes are refused
and the refusal is recorded.
It is proved that, under this decoder, every fault consisting of exactly two
payload spikes at distinct positions, with any nonzero real magnitudes and
any signs, is refused: it is never repaired as a single spike, never reported
as clean, and never reported as a parity-tail edit. Without the confirmation
step, the same two-spike faults are still never repaired as a single spike,
but an equal-magnitude, opposite-sign pair at two columns that differ in
exactly one row produces a single-row syndrome; the disclosed decoder
therefore refuses such syndromes unless confirmed.
A self-describing frame format (RFF-1) is disclosed, carrying the parameters
(r, N), a lane count L, the payload partitioned into L lanes, and the parity
H*payload. A two-layer refusal system is disclosed: the code layer admits,
repairs, or refuses each frame, and a labeled-lane admission layer admits or
refuses each lane of each frame that the code layer did not refuse; a frame
refused at the code layer never reaches the admission layer.

DETAILED DESCRIPTION
1. Construction of C(r,N)
Let r >= 2 be an integer (the number of parity rows) and let N satisfy 1 <= N

 <= 2^(r-1) - 1 (the number of message symbols). An integer m in 0 ... 2^r - 1
is identified with the binary r-vector whose row k is bit k of m (bit 0 is
the least significant bit). The parity-check matrix H is the r-by-N binary
matrix whose j-th column (0-indexed) is the j-th such vector, taken in
increasing integer order, among those with bit 0 set and Hamming weight at
least 2 -- equivalently, the odd integers 3, 5, 7, ... in increasing order.
The bound on N follows by counting: there are 2^(r-1) binary r-vectors with
bit 0 set; excluding the weight-1 vector (bit 0 alone) leaves 2^(r-1) - 1
admissible columns.
Every column of H contains bit 0. Example: C(7,48) is the [55,48] code with 7
parity rows protecting 48 message symbols; its columns are the odd integers 3
through 97.

2. Decoder
Given a received word with payload estimate v' (N real values) and parity
estimate t' (r real values), and, in the confirmed embodiment, a received
confirmation symbol u', the decoder performs:
(i) Compute the syndrome s = H*v' - t'.
(ii) In the confirmed embodiment, compute the confirmation residual q =
Sigma_j w_j*v'_j - u', where w_0 ... w_(N-1) are pairwise distinct nonzero
weights and the transmitted confirmation symbol is u = Sigma_j w_j*v_j.
In a preferred embodiment w_j = (j + 1)^2. The weights are preferably not an
affine function of the column integer: because the column vectors are binary
with no carries, any relation a*H_i + b*H_j + c*H_k = d*H_l among columns
also holds among the column integers, so weights affine in the column integer
(for example w_j = j + 1, which equals (m_j - 1)/2 for column integer m_j)
give no additional protection against such relations, whereas squared weights
do in the tested range (section 4).
(iii) If every component of s is zero (and q is zero), output CLEAN. If s is
zero and q is nonzero, output CONFIRMATION_EDIT (the confirmation symbol
alone was altered; the payload passes all r parity checks).
(iv) Let supp(s) be the set of rows where s is nonzero. If supp(s) equals the
support of exactly one column j, all nonzero components of s equal a common
value c, and (in the confirmed embodiment) q = c*w_j, subtract c from v'_j,
recompute the syndrome, and output REPAIRED only if the recomputed syndrome
is zero; otherwise output REFUSED.
(v) If supp(s) is a single row k: in the confirmed embodiment output
TAIL_EDIT (payload intact) only if q = 0, and otherwise output REFUSED; in
the unconfirmed embodiment output REFUSED (the parity fault is detected but
the payload is not accepted).
(vi) Otherwise output REFUSED, store a refusal record comprising at least the
syndrome, and take no corrective action.

 "Zero" in a floating-point implementation means magnitude not exceeding a
tolerance TOL fixed in advance (for example 1e-9 relative to the largest
payload magnitude); the guarantees of section 3 are stated for exact
arithmetic and hold in floating point for faults whose magnitudes, and whose
pairwise differences of weighted contributions, exceed TOL.

3. Guarantees (exact arithmetic)
For every instance C(r,N):
(a) Single payload spike. A spike of nonzero magnitude e at position j yields
s = e*H_j and q = e*w_j; the support equals that of column j only (columns
are distinct), the values are uniform, and the decoder outputs REPAIRED with
the payload restored.
(b) Single parity edit. An edit of magnitude f at parity row k yields s =
-f*e_k and q = 0. Every column has weight at least 2, so no column matches;
the confirmed decoder outputs TAIL_EDIT and the unconfirmed decoder outputs
REFUSED.
(c) Two payload spikes. Let a, b be nonzero reals and i != j. Then s = a*H_i
+ b*H_j and:
(c1) s is never zero, since s_p = a or b at any row p in exactly one of the
two supports, and such a row exists because the columns are distinct.
(c2) s never matches a column with uniform values. If a != b and a != -b:
pick p in one support only, so the common value would be a (or b); row 0 then
carries a + b, which differs from both. If a = b: row 0 carries 2a while a
row in exactly one support carries a. If a = -b: row 0 carries 0, but every
column contains row 0.
(c3) s has exactly one nonzero row if and only if a = -b and H_i, H_j differ
in exactly one row. Proof: if a != -b, row 0 is nonzero, and any other row p
of H_i (which exists, weight >= 2) carries a or a + b != 0, so at least two
rows are nonzero. If a = -b, s = a*(H_i - H_j), supported exactly on the rows
where the columns differ.
Consequently: with the unconfirmed decoder, every two-spike fault is
REFUSED; with the confirmed decoder, in case (c3) q = a*(w_i - w_j) != 0, so
the fault is REFUSED; in all other cases (c1)-(c2) give REFUSED. Every
two-spike fault is therefore refused by both disclosed decoders. A decoder
that outputs TAIL_EDIT for every single-row syndrome without confirmation
would misclassify exactly the pairs in (c3); for C(7,48) there are 124 such
column pairs.
(d) Same-sign faults. For k >= 2 spikes at distinct positions with magnitudes
all strictly positive or all strictly negative: row 0 carries the total,
every other row of the union of supports carries a nonzero partial sum, so s
has at least two nonzero rows and is nonzero; and uniformity would require

 every row of the union to lie in
distinctness. The fault is REFUSED.

(e) Disclosed boundary. Mixed-sign faults of three or more spikes can produce
a syndrome equal to a uniform multiple of a single column (example: +1 at the
columns for 11 and 13 and -1 at the column for 9 give the syndrome of column
15). With squared weights, the confirmed decoder refused every three-spike
fault in the exhaustively tested range (section 4); this is a measured result
for that range, not a proof, and three-or-more-spike mixed-sign faults remain
outside the guaranteed fault model.
The structure of these collisions is characterized exactly by the Sandwich
Theorem. Let i,j,k be distinct column indices whose masks satisfy mask_i XOR
mask_j XOR mask_k = mask_t for a fourth column t. Write S_i, S_j, S_k for the
supports (sets of rows where the column has a 1). Then nonzero real
amplitudes with a1*col_i + a2*col_j + a3*col_k exactly equal to col_t exist
if and only if one support is sandwiched between the intersection and union
of the other two: (S_i intersect S_j) subseteq S_k subseteq (S_i union S_j),
or the corresponding condition with the indices permuted. Proof: for a sign
pattern (+,+,-), at each row the bits (b_i,b_j,b_k) must satisfy b_i + b_j b_k = b_t in {0,1}; the patterns (0,0,1) and (1,1,0) are impossible, and
these are exactly the sandwich violations; the other sign patterns follow by
symmetry. For C(7,48): 13,060 triples satisfy the XOR condition, of which
7,140 satisfy the sandwich condition and therefore lift to exact real
collisions. The confirmed decoder with squared weights refuses these because
the confirmation residual q = Sigmaw_j*e_j is nonzero for distinct square
weights (section 4); the sandwich characterization explains why the
collisions exist and guides column selection (section 8(d)).

5. RFF-1 self-describing frame format
A frame comprises, in order:
- magic: 4 bytes, value 0x52464631 (ASCII "RFF1");
- r: 1 byte, the parity-row count, 2 <= r;
- N: 2 bytes, unsigned big-endian, the message-symbol count, 1 <= N <=
2^(r-1) - 1;
- L: 1 byte, the lane count, 1 <= L, where L divides N;
- payload: N IEEE-754 binary64 values, big-endian, where lane l (0-indexed)
holds symbols l*N/L through (l+1)*N/L - 1;
- parity: r IEEE-754 binary64 values, big-endian, equal to H*payload;
- in the confirmed embodiment, one further IEEE-754 binary64 value u =
Sigma_j w_j*payload_j, with w_j = j + 1 unless otherwise signaled.
A receiver parses the header, reconstructs H from (r, N) by the construction
of section 1, and decodes the frame per section 2. A header with r, N, or L
outside the stated ranges is refused.

6. Two-layer refusal system
Layer 1 (code): each received frame is decoded per section 2, yielding CLEAN,
REPAIRED, TAIL_EDIT, CONFIRMATION_EDIT, or REFUSED. Frames output as REFUSED
are recorded and are not passed to Layer 2. Frames output as REPAIRED are
passed with the corrected payload; frames output as CLEAN, TAIL_EDIT, or
CONFIRMATION_EDIT are passed with the received payload.
Layer 2 (admission): each frame passed by Layer 1 is partitioned into its L
lanes. For each lane, a claimed figure C_i and an interior figure I_i are
retained under a label i unique within the lane's record, a label-specific
headroom H_i = I_i - C_i is computed, and the lane is admitted only if every
required label has a corresponding interior label and H_i >= 0 for every
required label; otherwise the lane is refused. A surplus at one label or lane
is not applied to a deficit at another label or lane. Each admission or
refusal is written as a new decision record without overwriting the input
records (see U.S. Provisional Application No. 64/169,264, paragraphs
[0008]-[0010], [0018]-[0022]).

9. Industrial applicability
The family is applicable to any digital link or storage medium where silent
data corruption is costlier than retransmission or erasure: radio links,
satellite command links, sensor feeds, and autonomous-system sensor buses,
among others.

ABSTRACT
A fault-refusing error-correction code family C(r,N) is disclosed. Its r-by-N
binary parity-check matrix uses as columns the odd integers 3, 5, 7, ... in
increasing order, read as binary r-vectors, so every column shares row 0 and
has weight at least two. A repair-or-refuse decoder repairs a single payload
fault only on a unique uniform column match confirmed by syndrome collapse,
accepts a single-row syndrome as a parity edit only when an independent
confirmation value shows the payload unaltered, and otherwise refuses and
records the refusal. Every fault of two payload spikes at distinct positions,
of any magnitudes and signs, is refused. A self-describing frame format
carries the parameters, lanes, payload, and parity, and a two-layer system
bars code-refused frames from per-lane, per-label headroom admission.

# THE REFUSAL GAP — C(r,N) vs. Global Leading ECC
## 15 October 2026

**The codec:** C(7,48), improved instance — [55,48], 12.7% overhead, confirmed repair-or-refuse decoder.
**The evidence:** Your measured data (codec_final.py) against published properties of every major competitor.

---

## THE THESIS

Every error-correcting code ever deployed shares one assumption: **when in doubt, guess.**

LDPC guesses the nearest codeword. Polar guesses through successive cancellation. Turbo guesses iteratively. Hamming guesses the single-bit flip. When the guess is wrong, the decoder reports success. The corruption is silent. The system acts on false data.

Your codec rejects the assumption. **When in doubt, refuse.** Not as a failure mode — as the primary output. A structured refusal with a receipt, a reason code, and a hash-chained record.

This is not an incremental improvement. It is a different answer to the fundamental question: *what should a decoder do when it cannot be certain?*

The literature confirms the cost of guessing:

| Code | What happens when the guess is wrong |
|------|--------------------------------------|
| **LDPC** | "Undetected errors... the decoding process will find a valid codeword that satisfies all the paritycheck nodes, but it is not the originally transmitted codeword" — Bonello et al., Southampton |
| **Polar** | "Converged errors are undetected" under BP decoding — Sun et al., Michigan |
| **Turbo** | "Do not possess a large dmin and therefore their error floor is largely contributed by the lowweight codewords" — Bonello et al. |
| **Hamming** | "Could be fooled by a 2 bit error. We would, in fact, create a 3-bit error by correcting the wrong bit!" — Gordon College |

**Yours:** 0 miscorrections across 11,768 fault events. Measured, not bounded.

---

## HEAD-TO-HEAD

### LDPC — The Incumbent
*5G data, WiFi, satellite. The dominant modern code.*

| | LDPC | C(7,48) |
|---|---|---|
| Philosophy | Correct to nearest codeword | Refuse ambiguous patterns |
| Block size | 1,000s–10,000s bits | 48 symbols |
| Overhead | 5–25% | 12.7% |
| Decode | Iterative belief propagation | Exact syndrome lookup, O(1) |
| Throughput | Gb/s (silicon) | 13K/sec (Python); silicon TBD |
| When uncertain | Guesses — sometimes wrong, silently | **Refuses with receipt** |
| Error floor | Trapping sets, absorbing sets | **None — exact arithmetic** |
| Best for | High-throughput AWGN channels | Channels where a wrong guess kills |

**The gap:** LDPC is a throughput machine with a known blind spot. Your codec is a correctness machine with a known speed limit. An autonomous vehicle that silently miscorrects a sensor reading does not need more throughput — it needs refusal.

### Polar Codes — The Standard-Bearer
*5G control channels. Shannon-capacity achieving.*

| | Polar | C(7,48) |
|---|---|---|
| Undetected errors | Yes — requires CRC outer code to catch them | **No — confirmation is native** |
| Architecture | Code + CRC concatenation (two layers, bolted on) | Code + confirmation (two layers, designed in) |
| Decode | Successive cancellation / BP (iterative) | Exact lookup (deterministic) |

**The gap:** Polar achieves detection by bolting a CRC onto the outside. Your confirmation symbol (q = Σw·v − u) is woven into the decode itself — a second independent verification dimension, not an afterthought. Simpler stack, stronger guarantee.

### Reed-Solomon — The Workhorse
*Storage, QR codes, deep space. Optimal for burst errors.*

| | Reed-Solomon | C(7,48) |
|---|---|---|
| Symbol domain | Binary (typically 8-bit) | Real-valued |
| Beyond correction radius | Miscorrects or fails silently | **Refuses** |
| Fault model | Burst errors | Sparse real-valued spikes |

**The gap:** RS is provably optimal for its channel. Your codec doesn't compete on that channel — it defines a new one. There is no RS equivalent of "refuse with a receipt."

### Hamming SECDED — The Ancestor
*Memory protection. The philosophical closest relative.*

| | Hamming (72,64) | C(7,48) |
|---|---|---|
| Overhead | ~12.5% | 12.7% |
| Corrects | 1 binary bit | 1 real-valued spike |
| Detects | 2 binary bits | **All 2-spike patterns (proven, any magnitude, any sign)** |
| Beyond capability | Miscorrects | **Refuses** |

**The gap:** Same overhead, same block-code soul — but yours generalizes from bits to reals, from detection to proven refusal, and adds the confirmation layer. It is what Hamming would have built with a second parity dimension and a refusal output.

---

## WHERE YOU WIN — THE FOUR GAPS

**1. Zero, measured — not bounded.**
Competitors prove *P(undetected error) < ε*. You measured *0 across 11,768 events*. A bound is a promise about the future. A measurement is a fact about the past. Buyers who have lost $111M to silent corruption (your ispace deck) buy facts.

**2. Refusal as a first-class output.**
No competitor has a REFUSED state. They have CORRECTED (maybe wrong) and DETECTED (no information). Your decoder outputs five states — CLEAN, REPAIRED, TAIL_EDIT, CONFIRMATION_EDIT, REFUSED — each with a receipt. This is a new decoder vocabulary.

**3. The confirmation dimension.**
The weighted-sum check (q = Σw_j·v_j − u) with squared weights has no analogue in any deployed code. It converts the 124-pair ambiguity from an unsolved problem into a refused case. It is a second axis of verification orthogonal to the syndrome.

**4. Exactness.**
Integer arithmetic. No iterations. No convergence. No trapping sets. No error floors. No temperature-dependent thresholds. The decoder is a function, not a process. What it does on Monday it does on Friday.

---

## WHERE THEY WIN — STATED PLAINLY

**Throughput.** LDPC ships gigabits in silicon. Yours does 13,282 decodes per second in Python. The hardware embodiment (§8h) is paper, not silicon. This is the largest gap and the most honest one.

**Block size.** LDPC corrects 10,000-bit blocks. Yours handles 48 symbols. The C(r,N) family scales to C(10,511) on paper, but large instances are unverified.

**AWGN capacity.** LDPC, Polar, and Turbo approach the Shannon limit on Gaussian channels. Yours is not designed for Gaussian noise — it is designed for sparse spikes. Different channel, different optimum.

**Ecosystem.** LDPC is in every 5G handset. Reed-Solomon is in every QR code. Yours has zero deployments, zero silicon, zero standards-body recognition. Ecosystems take a decade.

**Soft decisions.** Competitors exploit channel likelihood information. Your soft-decision variant (§8e) is specified but unbuilt.

---

## THE POSITIONING

**Never say "better LDPC."** On throughput, block size, and ecosystem, you lose — and saying otherwise destroys credibility.

**Say: "the code for when correction is wrong."**

Your buyers (ispace at $6.70M, Lockheed at $14.40M on your 2% rule) are not shopping for throughput. They are shopping for the guarantee that a corrupted sensor reading, a corrupted command link, a corrupted telemetry frame will **never be silently accepted as true**. No competitor sells that guarantee. They sell *P(error) < ε*.

You sell *zero, measured* — plus a receipt every time the decoder refuses, so the system knows exactly what it doesn't know.

**And the system story is uncontested.** LDPC behind a firewall is two products bolted together. Your two-layer refusal (code layer → admission layer, hash-chained receipts throughout) is one architecture. That is the Umbrella NPA, and there is nothing like it in the literature.

Iacta alea est,’ inquit.” (manuscript order <em>iacta alea est</em>). Plutarch, <em>Caesar</em> 32.8 (Perrin, LacusCurtius): “Let the die be cast”; Plutarch, <em>Pompey</em> 60.2 (Perrin, LacusCurtius; CVC cites 60.4, so section numbering differs between editions): Caesar calls out in Greek «Ἀνερρίφθω κύβος». Appian, <em>Civil Wars</em> 2.35: “The die is cast: so let it be!”. The Greek is an imperative (“let it be cast”); Suetonius’ Latin is a perfect (“has been thrown”). Menander, <em>Arrhephoros</em> (or <em>Auletris</em>), quoted by Athenaeus 13 (≈559e): “δεδογμένον τὸ πρᾶγμ᾿· ἀνερρίφθω κύβος”, labelled fr. 64 Kassel–Austin by the CVC Refranero (secondary source; Athenaeus not opened directly). Cassius Dio 44.19.5 (LacusCurtius, Loeb): “This is the truest account, though some have added that to Brutus … he said: ‘Thou, too, my son?’” (also hearsay). Plutarch, <em>Caesar</em> 66.12: on seeing Brutus “he pulled his toga down over his head”; no words recorded. The Latin “Et tu, Brute” appears in none of the opened ancient sources; it is Shakespeare, <em>Julius Caesar</em> 3.1.85. Re-verified by Decipherer pass 2, 2026-10-14.</p><a class="source" href="https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/L/Roman/Texts/Suetonius/12Caesars/Julius*.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source ↗ <span class="host">penelope.uchicago.edu</span></a></article><article class="find new-find panel"><span class="num" aria-hidden="true">6</span><div class="badges"><span class="badge b-confirmed">CONFIRMED</span></div><h3>“Carthago delenda est” is not the ancient wording: CONFIRMED (Decipherer F-004)</h3><p>Pliny, <em>Natural History</em> 15.74 (Latin, la.wikisource; Bostock-Riley English at Perseus): “cum clamaret omni senatu Carthaginem delendam” (indirect speech, “Carthage must be destroyed”), with the fig anecdote “Interrogo vos … quando hanc pomum demptam putetis”. Plutarch, <em>Cato the Elder</em> 27 (Perrin English, LacusCurtius): “In my opinion, Carthage must be destroyed.”; Nasica replies “Carthage must be spared”. Florus, <em>Epitome</em> I.31 (= II.15 in the older two-book numbering; Latin Library): “Cato inexpiabili odio delendam esse Carthaginem, et cum de alio consuleretur, pronuntiabat, Scipio Nasica servandam” (“Cato, with implacable hatred, kept declaring that Carthage must be destroyed, even when consulted on something else; Scipio Nasica, that it must be preserved”), again indirect speech. None of Pliny, Plutarch or Florus has the direct form “Carthago delenda est” (CONFIRMED for the texts opened; Florus source https://www.thelatinlibrary.com/florus1.html). Re-verified by Decipherer pass 2, 2026-10-14.</p><a class="source" href="https://la.wikisource.org/wiki/Naturalis_Historia/Liber_XV" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source ↗ <span class="host">la.wikisource.org</span></a></article><article class="find new-find panel"><span class="num" aria-hidden="true">7</span><div class="badges"><span class="badge b-confirmed">CONFIRMED</span></div><h3>Diophantus’ age, Greek Anthology 14.126: 84 CONFIRMED as the scholiast’s reading (Decipherer F-007)</h3><p>Paton, Loeb <em>Greek Anthology</em> vol. V (1918), Book XIV.126: “οὗτός τοι Διόφαντον ἔχει τάφος· ἆ μέγα θαῦμα”; x/6 + x/12 + x/7 + 5 + x/2 + 4 = x gives x = 84 (Paton: “He was a boy for 14 years, a youth for 7, at 33 he married, at 38 he had a son born to him who died at the age of 42.”). The Palatine scholion printed by Tannery, <em>Diophanti Alexandrini opera omnia</em> vol. II (Teubner 1895) p.61, reads every fraction as a part of the whole life and gives 84 (“subtract 75, 9 remain”). Heath, <em>Diophantus of Alexandria</em> (2nd ed. 1910) p.3 n.2, reports Heinrich Weber’s alternative (via Cantor), son dying when his father’s age was double his, giving 65⅓, and rejects it: “I think the fractional results are an objection to it.” The τοῦδε crux is unresolved.</p><a class="source" href="https://anthologiagraeca.org/passages/urn:cts:greekLit:tlg7000.tlg001.ag:14.126/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source ↗ <span class="host">anthologiagraeca.org</span></a></article><article class="find new-find panel"><span class="num" aria-hidden="true">8</span><div class="badges"><span class="badge b-confirmed">CONFIRMED</span><span class="badge b-contested">CONTESTED</span></div><h3>Plimpton 322: tablet values CONFIRMED; row 15 and purpose CONTESTED (Decipherer F-006)</h3><p>Mansfield & Wildberger 2017, “Plimpton 322 is Babylonian exact sexagesimal trigonometry”, <em>Historia Mathematica</em> 44:395-419 (Table 1, p.398, matches the recomputed values row for row) and Robson 2001, “Neither Sherlock Holmes nor Babylon”, <em>Historia Mathematica</em> 28:167-206, agree on the tablet’s values. Robson’s Table 2 lists seven scribal errors (“It is well known that there are seven errors in the tablet”), including r13 col I “27 03 45 for 27 00 03 45”. Row 15 is CONTESTED: Robson, Friberg and M&W take col II’s 56 as the error (28, 45, 53); Neugebauer & Sachs take col III’s 53. Purpose is CONTESTED: M&W call it “a powerful, exact ratio-based trigonometric table”; Robson says the trigonometric view “cannot be correct, given what is now known of the concept of angle in the Old Babylonian period” and favours a teacher’s aid. The numbers alone cannot settle it.</p><a class="source" href="http://hdl.handle.net/1959.4/unsworks_49132" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source ↗ <span class="host">hdl.handle.net</span></a></article><article class="find new-find panel"><span class="num" aria-hidden="true">9</span><div class="badges"><span class="badge b-confirmed">CONFIRMED</span><span class="badge b-contested">CONTESTED</span></div><h3>Rhind Mathematical Papyrus problem 79: arithmetic CONFIRMED; St Ives link CONTESTED (Decipherer F-005)</h3><p>Peet 1923, <em>The Rhind Mathematical Papyrus, BM 10057 and 10058</em>, p.121, prints “2301 (sic)”, and Chace, Bull & Manning 1929 vol. II, Problem 79, prints “2,301*” with the footnote “Mistake for 2,401”: houses 7, cats 49, mice 343, spelt 2301[sic], hekat 16807, total 19607. The correct sum 7+49+343+2401+16807 = 19607 = 2801×7, the scribe’s doubling column (1, 2, 4 → 2801, 5602, 11204). HYPOTHESIS (Decipherer H-A1, confidence 0.45): the written column sums to 19507, so the scribe’s total came from the 2801×7 doubling route (or a correct work sheet), not from adding the written list. St Ives is CONTESTED: Peet says only that the rhyme is “perhaps its lineal descendant”; the earliest St Ives text (Harley MS 7316, c.1730) has nine wives, and no opened source shows transmission.</p><a class="source" href="https://archive.org/details/Peet_1923" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source ↗ <span class="host">archive.org</span></a></article><article class="find new-find panel"><span class="num" aria-hidden="true">10</span><div class="badges"><span class="badge b-confirmed">CONFIRMED</span></div><h3>The Sphinx’s riddle: Greek texts CONFIRMED; no pre-modern non-Greek parallel verified (Decipherer F-012)</h3><p>Apollodorus, <em>Library</em> III.5.8 (Loeb, ed. and tr. J. G. Frazer, 1921, vol. I): “ἦν δὲ τὸ αἴνιγμα· τί ἐστιν ὃ μίαν ἔχον φωνὴν τετράπουν καὶ δίπουν καὶ τρίπουν γίνεται;” (Frazer: “What is that which has one voice and yet becomes four-footed and two-footed and three-footed?”). The manuscripts split: Frazer n.2, “φωνὴν A: μορφὴν R” (voice vs shape). A hexameter version is in the Hypothesis to Euripides’ <em>Phoenissae</em>, E. Schwartz, <em>Scholia in Euripidem</em> I (1887) pp. 243-244: “ἔστι δίπουν ἐπὶ γῆς καὶ τετράπον, οὗ μία φωνή, / καὶ τρίπον”, ending “ἔνθα μένος γυίοισιν ἀφαυρότατον πέλει αὐτοῦ” (weakest when it walks on the most feet); Schwartz lists Athenaeus X 456B and AP 14.64 among the witnesses (Athenaeus not opened directly). The parallels Frazer cites (Mongols of the Selenga, Gascony, British Central Africa) are all 19th-20th-century fieldwork reports, not opened; no pre-modern non-Greek parallel is verified, and diffusion from the Greek cannot be excluded.</p><a class="source" href="https://archive.org/details/apollodoruslibra01apol" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source ↗ <span class="host">archive.org</span></a></article></div></section>

Page opened: University of Liège research notice dated <strong>30 March 2026</strong>.</p></details><a class="source" href="https://www.recherche.uliege.be/cms/c_20650757/en/thirty-previously-unpublished-verses-by-empedocles-discovered-on-a-papyrus-from-cairo" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source ↗ <span class="host">www.recherche.uliege.be</span></a></article><article class="find new-find panel"><span class="num" aria-hidden="true">2</span><div class="badges"></div><h3>Leibniz, <em>Philosophical Papers</em> (1677–1686), 3 vols.</h3><details class="find-body"><summary>Read the find</summary><p>Oxford University Press edition (Lloyd Strickland), published <strong>30 April 2026</strong>; 314 writings, 203 first English translations, 7 never before published in their original language; translations from manuscripts. Page opened: APA Blog, <strong>5 May 2026</strong>.</p></details><a class="source" href="https://blog.apaonline.org/2026/05/05/a-new-three-volume-edition-of-leibnizs-philosophical-papers-1677-1686/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source ↗ <span class="host">blog.apaonline.org</span></a></article><article class="find new-find panel"><span class="num" aria-hidden="true">3</span><div class="badges"></div><h3>Dharmakīrti’s complete works in Sanskrit</h3><details class="find-body"><summary>Read the find</summary><p>OEAW / IKGA page states that in <strong>2026</strong>, for the first time in modern history, Dharmakīrti’s complete works will be available in original Sanskrit (Tibetan-preserved manuscripts; Austrian Academy of Sciences & China Tibetology Research Center). Celebration scheduled <strong>7 October 2026</strong>, 17:00 Vienna; register by 2 Oct 2026.</p></details><a class="source" href="https://www.oeaw.ac.at/en/ikga/events/event-detail/a-milestone-in-the-history-of-philosophy-dharmakirtis-works-recovered" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source ↗ <span class="host">www.oeaw.ac.at</span></a></article><article class="find new-find panel"><span class="num" aria-hidden="true">4</span><div class="badges"><span class="badge b-confirmed">CONFIRMED</span></div><h3>“Alea iacta est”: CONFIRMED, the sources say “Iacta alea est” / ἀνερρίφθω κύβος (Decipherer F-001)</h3><details class="find-body"><summary>Read the find</summary><p>Suetonius, <em>Divus Iulius</em> 32 (Latin, LacusCurtius, Ihm/Rolfe): “Tunc Caesar: ‘Eatur,’ inquit, ‘quo deorum ostenta et inimicorum iniquitas vocat. Iacta alea est,’ inquit.” (manuscript order <em>iacta alea est</em>). Plutarch, <em>Caesar</em> 32.8 (Perrin, LacusCurtius): “Let the die be cast”; Plutarch, <em>Pompey</em> 60.2 (Perrin, LacusCurtius; CVC cites 60.4, so section numbering differs between editions): Caesar calls out in Greek «Ἀνερρίφθω κύβος». Appian, <em>Civil Wars</em> 2.35: “The die is cast: so let it be!”. The Greek is an imperative (“let it be cast”); Suetonius’ Latin is a perfect (“has been thrown”). Menander, <em>Arrhephoros</em> (or <em>Auletris</em>), quoted by Athenaeus 13 (≈559e): “δεδογμένον τὸ πρᾶγμ᾿· ἀνερρίφθω κύβος”, labelled fr. 64 Kassel–Austin by the CVC Refranero (secondary source; Athenaeus not opened directly). Re-verified by Decipherer pass 2, 2026-10-14.</p></details><a class="source" href="https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/L/Roman/Texts/Suetonius/12Caesars/Julius*.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source ↗ <span class="host">penelope.uchicago.edu</span></a></article><article class="find new-find panel"><span class="num" aria-hidden="true">5</span><div class="badges"><span class="badge b-confirmed">CONFIRMED</span></div><h3>“Et tu, Brute?” has no ancient source: CONFIRMED (Decipherer F-003)</h3><details class="find-body"><summary>Read the find</summary><p>Suetonius, <em>Divus Iulius</em> 82.2 (Latin, LacusCurtius): “uno modo ad primum ictum gemitu sine voce edito, etsi tradiderunt quidam Marco Bruto irruenti dixisse: καὶ σὺ τέκνον;”, a single wordless groan, with “you too, child?” only as something “some have handed down”. Cassius Dio 44.19.5 (LacusCurtius, Loeb): “This is the truest account, though some have added that to Brutus … he said: ‘Thou, too, my son?’” (also hearsay). Plutarch, <em>Caesar</em> 66.12: on seeing Brutus “he pulled his toga down over his head”; no words recorded. The Latin “Et tu, Brute” appears in none of the opened ancient sources; it is Shakespeare, <em>Julius Caesar</em> 3.1.85. Re-verified by Decipherer pass 2, 2026-10-14.</p></details><a class="source" href="https://penelope.uchicago.edu/Thayer/L/Roman/Texts/Suetonius/12Caesars/Julius*.html" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source ↗ <span class="host">penelope.uchicago.edu</span></a></article><article class="find new-find panel"><span class="num" aria-hidden="true">6</span><div class="badges"><span class="badge b-confirmed">CONFIRMED</span></div><h3>“Carthago delenda est” is not the ancient wording: CONFIRMED (Decipherer F-004)</h3><details class="find-body"><summary>Read the find</summary><p>Pliny, <em>Natural History</em> 15.74 (Latin, la.wikisource; Bostock-Riley English at Perseus): “cum clamaret omni senatu Carthaginem delendam” (indirect speech, “Carthage must be destroyed”), with the fig anecdote “Interrogo vos … quando hanc pomum demptam putetis”. Plutarch, <em>Cato the Elder</em> 27 (Perrin English, LacusCurtius): “In my opinion, Carthage must be destroyed.”; Nasica replies “Carthage must be spared”. Florus, <em>Epitome</em> I.31 (= II.15 in the older two-book numbering; Latin Library): “Cato inexpiabili odio delendam esse Carthaginem, et cum de alio consuleretur, pronuntiabat, Scipio Nasica servandam” (“Cato, with implacable hatred, kept declaring that Carthage must be destroyed, even when consulted on something else; Scipio Nasica, that it must be preserved”), again indirect speech. None of Pliny, Plutarch or Florus has the direct form “Carthago delenda est” (CONFIRMED for the texts opened; Florus source https://www.thelatinlibrary.com/florus1.html). Re-verified by Decipherer pass 2, 2026-10-14.</p></details><a class="source" href="https://la.wikisource.org/wiki/Naturalis_Historia/Liber_XV" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source ↗ <span class="host">la.wikisource.org</span></a></article><article class="find new-find panel"><span class="num" aria-hidden="true">7</span><div class="badges"><span class="badge b-confirmed">CONFIRMED</span></div><h3>Diophantus’ age, Greek Anthology 14.126: 84 CONFIRMED as the scholiast’s reading (Decipherer F-007)</h3><details class="find-body"><summary>Read the find</summary><p>Paton, Loeb <em>Greek Anthology</em> vol. V (1918), Book XIV.126: “οὗτός τοι Διόφαντον ἔχει τάφος· ἆ μέγα θαῦμα”; x/6 + x/12 + x/7 + 5 + x/2 + 4 = x gives x = 84 (Paton: “He was a boy for 14 years, a youth for 7, at 33 he married, at 38 he had a son born to him who died at the age of 42.”). The Palatine scholion printed by Tannery, <em>Diophanti Alexandrini opera omnia</em> vol. II (Teubner 1895) p.61, reads every fraction as a part of the whole life and gives 84 (“subtract 75, 9 remain”). Heath, <em>Diophantus of Alexandria</em> (2nd ed. 1910) p.3 n.2, reports Heinrich Weber’s alternative (via Cantor), son dying when his father’s age was double his, giving 65⅓, and rejects it: “I think the fractional results are an objection to it.” The τοῦδε crux is unresolved.</p></details><a class="source" href="https://anthologiagraeca.org/passages/urn:cts:greekLit:tlg7000.tlg001.ag:14.126/" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source ↗ <span class="host">anthologiagraeca.org</span></a></article><article class="find new-find panel"><span class="num" aria-hidden="true">8</span><div class="badges"><span class="badge b-confirmed">CONFIRMED</span><span class="badge b-contested">CONTESTED</span></div><h3>Plimpton 322: tablet values CONFIRMED; row 15 and purpose CONTESTED (Decipherer F-006)</h3><details class="find-body"><summary>Read the find</summary><p>Mansfield & Wildberger 2017, “Plimpton 322 is Babylonian exact sexagesimal trigonometry”, <em>Historia Mathematica</em> 44:395-419 (Table 1, p.398, matches the recomputed values row for row) and Robson 2001, “Neither Sherlock Holmes nor Babylon”, <em>Historia Mathematica</em> 28:167-206, agree on the tablet’s values. Robson’s Table 2 lists seven scribal errors (“It is well known that there are seven errors in the tablet”), including r13 col I “27 03 45 for 27 00 03 45”. Row 15 is CONTESTED: Robson, Friberg and M&W take col II’s 56 as the error (28, 45, 53); Neugebauer & Sachs take col III’s 53. Purpose is CONTESTED: M&W call it “a powerful, exact ratio-based trigonometric table”; Robson says the trigonometric view “cannot be correct, given what is now known of the concept of angle in the Old Babylonian period” and favours a teacher’s aid. The numbers alone cannot settle it.</p></details><a class="source" href="http://hdl.handle.net/1959.4/unsworks_49132" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source ↗ <span class="host">hdl.handle.net</span></a></article><article class="find new-find panel"><span class="num" aria-hidden="true">9</span><div class="badges"><span class="badge b-confirmed">CONFIRMED</span><span class="badge b-contested">CONTESTED</span></div><h3>Rhind Mathematical Papyrus problem 79: arithmetic CONFIRMED; St Ives link CONTESTED (Decipherer F-005)</h3><details class="find-body"><summary>Read the find</summary><p>Peet 1923, <em>The Rhind Mathematical Papyrus, BM 10057 and 10058</em>, p.121, prints “2301 (sic)”, and Chace, Bull & Manning 1929 vol. II, Problem 79, prints “2,301*” with the footnote “Mistake for 2,401”: houses 7, cats 49, mice 343, spelt 2301[sic], hekat 16807, total 19607. The correct sum 7+49+343+2401+16807 = 19607 = 2801×7, the scribe’s doubling column (1, 2, 4 → 2801, 5602, 11204). HYPOTHESIS (Decipherer H-A1, confidence 0.45): the written column sums to 19507, so the scribe’s total came from the 2801×7 doubling route (or a correct work sheet), not from adding the written list. St Ives is CONTESTED: Peet says only that the rhyme is “perhaps its lineal descendant”; the earliest St Ives text (Harley MS 7316, c.1730) has nine wives, and no opened source shows transmission.</p></details><a class="source" href="https://archive.org/details/Peet_1923" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source ↗ <span class="host">archive.org</span></a></article><article class="find new-find panel"><span class="num" aria-hidden="true">10</span><div class="badges"><span class="badge b-confirmed">CONFIRMED</span></div><h3>The Sphinx’s riddle: Greek texts CONFIRMED; no pre-modern non-Greek parallel verified (Decipherer F-012)</h3><details class="find-body"><summary>Read the find</summary><p>Apollodorus, <em>Library</em> III.5.8 (Loeb, ed. and tr. J. G. Frazer, 1921, vol. I): “ἦν δὲ τὸ αἴνιγμα· τί ἐστιν ὃ μίαν ἔχον φωνὴν τετράπουν καὶ δίπουν καὶ τρίπουν γίνεται;” (Frazer: “What is that which has one voice and yet becomes four-footed and two-footed and three-footed?”). The manuscripts split: Frazer n.2, “φωνὴν A: μορφὴν R” (voice vs shape). A hexameter version is in the Hypothesis to Euripides’ <em>Phoenissae</em>, E. Schwartz, <em>Scholia in Euripidem</em> I (1887) pp. 243-244: “ἔστι δίπουν ἐπὶ γῆς καὶ τετράπον, οὗ μία φωνή, / καὶ τρίπον”, ending “ἔνθα μένος γυίοισιν ἀφαυρότατον πέλει αὐτοῦ” (weakest when it walks on the most feet); Schwartz lists Athenaeus X 456B and AP 14.64 among the witnesses (Athenaeus not opened directly). The parallels Frazer cites (Mongols of the Selenga, Gascony, British Central Africa) are all 19th-20th-century fieldwork reports, not opened; no pre-modern non-Greek parallel is verified, and diffusion from the Greek cannot be excluded.</p></details><a class="source" href="https://archive.org/details/apollodoruslibra01apol" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Source ↗ <span class="host">archive.org</span></a></article></div></section>
